invariants.summary: A generator's character sanitization MUST NOT substitute `?` for a character it cannot encode: every character a bootcamper-authored deliverable can carry MUST map to an ASCII equivalent or be dropped deliberately.

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: A validator's non-zero exit MUST NOT by itself gate a Bootcamp step. Its findings MUST be classified into **structural invalidity** (the data cannot load — blocking) and **conformance to a recommendation** (the data loads and resolves but is not in the recommended shape — informational), and only the former may block. A conformance finding MUST NOT trigger remapping, rewriting or regenerating data that already loads; converting to the recommended shape may be offered as an optional improvement, never as remediation of a defect or a precondition for continuing. Where a tool's verdict and an authoritative specification **from the same source** disagree, the disagreement MUST be resolved empirically — load one unmodified record and read back the features Senzing extracted — and the probe result and concluded cause MUST be recorded (INV-125); it MUST NOT be settled by preferring one document over the other. Observed: `sz_json_analyzer.py` returns exit 1 with hundreds of "Missing or non-array FEATURES" errors, plus the warning `No NAME features found`, against data that loads and resolves identically to the recommended shape — the analyzer measures conformance to the *recommended* schema (whose validation rules do say `FEATURES` is required), while the specification's prose grants continued support for the legacy shape. Both statements are true and they answer different questions; a warning that a feature was not found where the tool looked MUST NOT be reported as that feature being absent. (Source: `analyzer-legacy-sublist-format-false-errors`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: A validator's non-zero exit MUST NOT by itself gate a Bootcamp step.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: A check on record shape MUST accept every shape the Senzing Entity Specification supports, not only the recommended one: currently the `FEATURES` array **and** the legacy flat structure — "a flat JSON structure with a separate sub-list for each feature that had multiple values", i.e. feature attributes at the record root with a per-feature root sub-list (`NAMES`, `ADDRESSES`, `IDENTIFIERS`) wherever a feature repeats, and no sub-list at all where no feature repeats. A source's shape MUST NOT be inferred from its provenance and MUST be determined by sampling the actual records: CORD ships both forms (verified 2026-07-26 — London/`GLOBALDATA` returns a `FEATURES` array, Las Vegas/`PPP_LOANS` returns flat root attributes). A readiness or fast-path gate keyed on `FEATURES` alone classifies loadable sources as not-ready and routes them through a mapping phase they do not need. (Source: `analyzer-legacy-sublist-format-false-errors`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: A check on record shape MUST accept every shape the Senzing Entity Specification supports, not only the recommended one: currently the `FEATURES` array **and** the legacy flat structure — "a flat JSON structure with a separate sub-list for each feature that had multiple values", i.e.

invariants.statement: Every screenshot a visualization capture produced MUST reach the recap. Because capture is one image per tab (INV-122), each file is already a distinct view, so a count cap or "best of" selection can only delete unique content — and any such judgment pulls toward the visually striking, which is what dropped Merge Statistics, Match Keys and Feature Scores (the three *analytical* tabs) from a six-tab app while the surrounding prose described all six, leaving the same three tabs repeated across two visualization sections. Only a true duplicate — two images of the **same** tab, which per-tab capture should not produce — may be deleted. This binds both the capture-time embed (`module-completion.md`) and graduation's orphaned-screenshot backfill; neither may cap, and the backfill in particular is the safety net for a missed embed, so capping it means it cannot restore what the capture step dropped. (Source: `embed-every-captured-tab-in-tab-order`, 2026-07-26.) (⚠️ **Closed INV-123's omission branch — recorded 2026-07-31, no meaning change here.** INV-123 permitted omitting an inert Search / Probe capture as an alternative to captioning it; this invariant had already made that unavailable, and the two shipped without either naming the other. INV-123's disjunction is now removed and the caption is its sole remedy. Nothing in this invariant changes: every screenshot the capture produced still MUST reach the recap, and a true same-tab duplicate is still the only deletable case.)
invariants.summary: Every screenshot a visualization capture produced MUST reach the recap.

invariants.statement: Screenshots MUST be embedded in the recap in the app's tab order — the row order of the tab table in `module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, which is declared there as the ordering authority — and never in capture, append or filename-discovery order. Both the capture-time embed and graduation's backfill MUST cite that table rather than restate the tab list, so changing a tab's position updates one file; a tab that produced no image is skipped without disturbing the relative order of the rest. Ordering the image lines a backfill itself produced is not a prose rewrite and does not violate the append-only rule (INV-085), which protects a completed section's narrative. The recap is a walkthrough of the app, so a reader must be able to line its images up against the interface left to right. (Source: `embed-every-captured-tab-in-tab-order`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: Screenshots MUST be embedded in the recap in the app's tab order — the row order of the tab table in `module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, which is declared there as the ordering authority — and never in capture, append or filename-discovery order.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: A **partially populated** parsed row MUST be treated as a probable wrong field name, not as partial data returned by Senzing: where some fields of a record populate and others come back blank, the blank ones' names MUST be confirmed against a dumped raw response before the row is rendered. A half-populated row is more deceptive than an empty one — the fields that did populate signal that the parse worked, so it reads as a real-but-thin result rather than a bug. Observed: `ENTITY_NETWORK_LINKS` entries parsed under the `ENTITY_ID` / `RELATED_ENTITY_ID` pairing used elsewhere yielded `None` for **both** endpoints while `MATCH_KEY` rendered correctly, presenting as a relationship Senzing could not fully describe. (Extends INV-115 from a single blank field to a partial record.) (Source: `network-link-fields-and-uncovered-response-schemas`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: A **partially populated** parsed row MUST be treated as a probable wrong field name, not as partial data returned by Senzing: where some fields of a record populate and others come back blank, the blank ones' names MUST be confirmed against a dumped raw response before the row is rendered.

invariants.statement: A `get_sdk_reference(topic='response_schemas')` result that is **empty** or that stops at the top-level shape is coverage, not a failed call: it MUST NOT be retried as an error, and the dumped raw response is the authority for anything below what it documents. Guidance that requires the lookup MUST state, at the point it requires it, what an empty or shallow result means — otherwise the reader retries a call that will never return more, or treats the top-level arrays as the whole answer. Verified 2026-07-26: `filter='find_network'` returned an entry documenting `ENTITY_PATHS[]`, `ENTITIES[]` and `ENTITY_NETWORK_LINKS[]` with **no** element fields, while `get_version` and `get_license` returned an empty `data` array. **Corrected in place 2026-07-29 (dry run, phase 1) — the first half no longer holds:** on server 1.32.1 `filter='find_network'` now returns the element fields itself (`ENTITY_NETWORK_LINKS[].MIN_ENTITY_ID`, `.MAX_ENTITY_ID`, `.MATCH_KEY`, `.MATCH_LEVEL_CODE`, `.ERRULE_CODE`, `.IS_AMBIGUOUS`, `.IS_DISCLOSED`, plus `ENTITIES[].RESOLVED_ENTITY.*` and `ENTITY_PATHS[].*`), so those names are MCP-confirmed and MUST NOT be carried as unverified cautions any longer; `get_version` still returns an empty `data` array, so the second half stands and remains the example of coverage-not-failure. **Both halves re-confirmed on server 1.32.9, 2026-08-13** (enumeration sweep): `filter='find_network'` still returns the element fields, and `filter='get_version'` still returns `"data": []`. **The rule this invariant states is unchanged** — an empty or shallow result is still coverage rather than a failed call, and a field name that *cannot* be MCP-confirmed still may not be written as the name to parse with. What changed is a dated observation about one method, which is exactly why the lookup must be re-run rather than quoted from here: this server's coverage grows. A field name that cannot be MCP-confirmed MUST NOT be written into guidance as the name to parse with; it may appear only as a marked, unverified caution about where to look (INV-080). (Clarifies INV-115's "does not reach" to cover absent as well as shallow coverage.) (Source: `network-link-fields-and-uncovered-response-schemas`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: A `get_sdk_reference(topic='response_schemas')` result that is **empty** or that stops at the top-level shape is coverage, not a failed call: it MUST NOT be retried as an error, and the dumped raw response is the authority for anything below what it documents.

invariants.statement: A note an MCP tool computes from a parameter the caller supplied is a **conditional**, not a measurement of this installation. Where the Bootcamp already holds a **detected** value for the same thing — the license record limit, the installed SDK version, the platform — the detected value governs: the generic note MUST be suppressed rather than relayed (INV-012, a warning the Bootcamper cannot act on is noise) and the divergence recorded in the checkpoint. This does NOT weaken INV-080: both sides remain MCP-sourced, one generically and one by measuring the Bootcamper's own machine, and answering from training data stays forbidden. Concretely: `sdk_guide`'s `record_count` contract states that values above 500 "surface license guidance (default Senzing license limit)" computed from the count alone, so that `LICENSE REQUIRED` note MUST be reconciled against `license_record_limit` (persisted by Module 4's license gate from `SzProduct.get_license()`) before it is relayed or acted on — `0` or a limit at/above the dataset size means suppress it entirely. Acting on it unreconciled sends a Bootcamper with an unlimited license to sample down to 500 records, and the shrunken dataset then under-demonstrates the cross-source resolution Modules 6 and 7 exist to show. (Source: `reconcile-sdk-guide-license-note-with-detected-limit`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: A note an MCP tool computes from a parameter the caller supplied is a **conditional**, not a measurement of this installation.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: The Bootcamp's redo drain MUST terminate. The loop sentinel MUST be the **fetch returning no record**, and a redo-*count* method MUST NOT be used as the loop condition — it is a full table scan per call, making the drain O(n²), and because processing a redo record generates more redo records the loop runs longer than the initial count suggests (384 backlog, 400 processed calls observed). Before running an MCP-returned redo snippet the guide MUST check whether it loops on an empty queue: the templates target streaming ingest, and the observed `sdk_guide(topic='redo')` answer prints a pause message and continues forever, so running it unmodified after a batch load hangs the session with no error — indistinguishable from slow work. If it loops, it MUST be adapted (keep the structure and concurrency, replace sleep-and-continue with a break). The drain MUST report how many records it processed and that the queue reached empty; a silent finish cannot be told from a hang. The production always-running processor MUST be described as the *streaming* pattern, explicitly distinguished from the batch drain. (Source: `redo-batch-drain-must-terminate`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: The Bootcamp's redo drain MUST terminate.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: The Senzing factory (environment) MUST outlive every engine it creates: a helper that constructs the factory in a local and returns only the engine returns a **dead** engine, because nothing keeps the factory alive. The resulting `SzSdkError - engine object has been destroyed and can no longer be used, create a new one` means *garbage-collected*, not explicitly destroyed, and surfaces at the first engine call far from the line that caused it. The factory MUST be held for the process lifetime or returned alongside whatever it created. Stated as ownership rather than a Python idiom (INV-002): however the chosen language expresses lifetime, the factory's MUST enclose every engine's. (Source: `factory-must-outlive-every-engine-it-creates`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: The Senzing factory (environment) MUST outlive every engine it creates: a helper that constructs the factory in a local and returns only the engine returns a **dead** engine, because nothing keeps the factory alive.

invariants.statement: A truncated label MUST remain distinguishable **wherever it appears and whatever it labels** — a bar-chart category, an entity name on a graph node, a legend entry, any future chart: **no two rendered labels may be identical unless their underlying values are identical**, the untruncated value MUST be reachable on hover, and truncation MUST NOT remove the leading characters. Distinctness MUST be checked by comparing the **fitted** strings, not the source values, and a pair that collides while its values differ MUST be disambiguated. Because a server generated in another language is built from `visualization-api-reference.md` and never reads the Python reference (INV-090/INV-124), this general rule MUST be stated in that contract as its own requirement and not only inside a rule about one label kind. (Scope clarified in place 2026-07-29 — no meaning change: this first clause was always unqualified, and the sentence about match keys below has always been an *application* of it rather than its extent. It had been implemented for match keys alone, so graph node labels sharing a 19-character prefix rendered identically on the one surface whose purpose is telling entities apart; `tests/test_graph_label_distinctness.py` now enforces the general property and MUST pass. Found by the 2026-07-28 deep-dive audit, scope settled by the maintainer 2026-07-29.) The label gutter MUST be sized from the data before anything is truncated, and a label MUST NOT be left to overflow and be clipped by the viewport — clipping removes the head of a right-anchored string, which is exactly the distinguishing part. For match keys, middle-ellipsis is required: they are `+A+B+C…` sequences that commonly share a long prefix and differ only in the final segment, so head-only truncation renders the top bars identically — the same unreadable chart failing from the other end. The distinctness property, not the ellipsis strategy, is the requirement. (Source: `visualization-legibility-at-production-scale`, 2026-07-26.)

A visualization default that governs legibility MUST be a function of the rendered data's scale, and the threshold MUST be stated as a number in the any-language contract so every implementation (INV-090) picks the same behavior. Above **400 entities** the Entity Graph MUST open on the relationship subgraph rather than the full population, provided a subgraph exists (`relationships_total` > 0); the mode toggle MUST still switch both ways, a Bootcamper's explicit choice MUST NOT be overridden by a later redraw, and an inline note MUST state both counts ("Showing the N entities that have relationships, of M total") for the same reason the label note exists — otherwise a default reads as the data. Hiding labels does not thin edges: at 4,464 relationships the full population conveys shape only. (Complements the scale-aware *label* defaults, which this extends to node selection.) (Source: `visualization-legibility-at-production-scale`, 2026-07-26.)
invariants.summary: A visualization default that governs legibility MUST be a function of the rendered data's scale, and the threshold MUST be stated as a number in the any-language contract so every implementation (INV-090) picks the same behavior.

invariants.statement: The consolidated visualization app's tab set is exactly **six**: Entity Graph, Merge Statistics, Match Keys, Feature Scores, Cross-Source, and Search / Probe — in the row order of the tab table in `module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, which remains the ordering authority (INV-147). The relationship-network view MUST be a **mode** of the Entity Graph tab (its "Show only entities with relationships" toggle, both modes served by the same `/api/graph` payload), and no-query merge browsing MUST be a **button** on Search / Probe ("Show all merged entities"); neither may be a tab of its own. There MUST be no Results Dashboard tab and no `/api/dashboard` endpoint — its counts and histogram duplicated `/api/stats`, which now also carries its only unique payload (`sample_entities`) — and `/api/records` MUST be served, since it backs the Records action every entity surface is required to offer. A tab is still shown only when its data exists. (This is INV-104's de-duplication rule applied to the enumeration in INV-104's own text: that list — written 2026-07-23 — named "relationship network" and "results dashboard" as tabs, and the consolidations that removed them registered no invariant, leaving the shipped six-tab app non-conformant with a still-standing invariant. INV-104's single-app, no-separate-static-pages, tab-only-when-data-exists and offer-counts-for-INV-046 guarantees are unchanged and still binding; only its tab enumeration is superseded. Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-27`, retroactively recording `consolidate-merge-statistics-and-results-dashboard-tabs` (2026-07-25) and `consolidate-truthset-viz-merges-and-network-tabs` (2026-07-26), 2026-07-27.)

The recap's Certificate of Completion MUST be laid out from the Senzing certificate template (`resources/certificate-of-completion.pdf`, a maintainer asset like the style reference behind `brand_tokens`): the ember gradient band, the bordered white card, the Senzing wordmark, the eyebrow, the headline, the tagline over its rule, the presented-to line, the recipient's name, the citation, the award seal, and the `DATE COMPLETED` / `ISSUED BY` signature blocks. Both renderers (INV-066) MUST read **one** shared set of geometry constants, so the fallback is a plainer *rendering* of that design and never a second design; every shared line MUST sit at the same height in both, verified positionally. The certificate MUST NOT claim more than the recap records: the citation states the number of modules **actually completed** (the template's "all 10 modules" is a claim about a full run) and any description of the bootcamp's arc attaches to the bootcamp, not to what was completed — while the modules completed remain named on the page (INV-100). The variable-length module list MUST be *fitted* — wider measure, then type size, truncation last — never allowed to print over the seal or the signature row, since the page is a fixed design with the auto page-break off. Letterspacing MUST be applied through the text state (`Tc`), never as spaces inserted between glyphs: a certificate is searched and copied out of, and "A l e x" is not a name. Colors MUST come from `brand_tokens` or be *derived* from it in the manner of `TABLE_HEAD_FILL` (INV-081/INV-107) — never sampled off the template — and where only the light wordmark ships it MUST be repainted for the white card at render time rather than duplicated as a second asset. Verification MUST be by rasterizing the page (INV-129). (Discharges the deferred template criterion of `landscape-certificate-of-completion`; complements INV-100, INV-113 and INV-126.) (Source: `certificate-of-completion-from-template`, 2026-07-28.)

The labeled blocks INV-103 requires inside each module's **End-of-Module Summary** — What you accomplished, Files produced, Why it matters (the "Bootcamper's takeaway" line stays optional) — MUST be enforced below the heading, not merely documented. `generate_recap_pdf.py`'s `--check` MUST fail naming each block a present summary does not carry, the pre-render audit MUST report the same gap as a warning (non-blocking: warn, render, exit 0 — INV-110/INV-048), and **both** renderers (INV-066) MUST *draw every required block*, marking one the recap does not carry as `(not recorded)` rather than omitting it — an absent block MUST NOT be able to look like a complete page. Detection MUST tolerate the forms a live recap produces (`**Label:**`, `**Label**:`, `- **Label:**`, a bare `Label:`), because a false "missing" sends graduation to backfill content that is already present or to rewrite a finished section (INV-085); legacy `### Journal` sections stay exempt, as INV-103 tolerates them. The requirement MUST also be stated where the recap is written (module-completion's recap step, verified in its existing re-read) and repaired before rendering (graduation's reconcile), and a backfill MUST NOT invent content to fill a label — an unsupported block is left for the renderer to mark. (INV-103 has required these blocks since 2026-07-23 and stated that `--check` must validate them; `--check` compared only H3 headings, so a summary written as one prose paragraph passed as "Recap complete", rendered at ~100% retention, and reached a bootcamper's keepsake with all three blocks absent. Reported from a bootcamp run 2026-07-28.) (Enforces INV-103; complements INV-110 and INV-129.) (Source: `end-of-module-summary-blocks-guaranteed`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: The labeled blocks INV-103 requires inside each module's **End-of-Module Summary** — What you accomplished, Files produced, Why it matters (the "Bootcamper's takeaway" line stays optional) — MUST be enforced below the heading, not merely documented.

invariants.statement: Wherever the SBCP directs the Bootcamper to act **in their Claude interface** — set a model, change reasoning effort, restart an MCP server, click a control — or documents how to install and start the bootcamp, it MUST name **which** interface, using these names: **Claude Desktop** (the desktop application), **Claude Code CLI** (Claude Code in a terminal), **the Claude web app**, **a Claude IDE extension**. "Claude Code" names the *product* and MUST NOT be used to mean an interface — it is correct for what is true of the harness everywhere (a Claude Code plugin, Claude Code hooks, an MCP server configured in Claude Code) and wrong as a synonym for the terminal, because Claude Desktop runs Claude Code too. **"The Claude app" / "the Claude application" is retired**: it named none of the four, so a Bootcamper told to use "your Claude app's model and effort controls" had to guess which controls were meant; it may appear only on a line that frames it as retired (`tests/test_retired_vocabulary.py`, which for this reason also scans the repo-root install docs `propagate-to-public` mirrors as user-facing). Vague wording ("in your Claude interface") is permitted **only** where the interface genuinely cannot be determined, never as a shortcut for one that can. The install docs MUST document both primary interfaces by name, state that they are two interfaces of one Claude Code plugin, and cross-link with anchors that resolve. This is a naming requirement only: the four interfaces INV-098 adapts to are unchanged, and INV-098's own wording was clarified in place to satisfy this. (Source: `name-the-claude-interface`, 2026-07-28.)

A generator MUST NOT reduce any character of a Bootcamper-authored value to `?`, and this MUST hold for the Bootcamper's **name** specifically — the string INV-134 detects from `git config user.name` and the Certificate of Completion prints largest. Characters outside the built-in fonts MUST be folded to a readable ASCII equivalent where one exists (including Latin letters with no NFKD decomposition — `Ł ł Đ đ Œ œ …`, whose loss changes the name rather than degrading it) and otherwise **dropped**, never encoded. A name in a non-Latin script MUST NOT be transliterated by the plugin: how it is spelled in Latin script is the Bootcamper's decision, so the generator MUST instead (a) warn on stderr naming the unprintable characters, (b) print the `CERTIFICATE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER` rather than a blank recipient line, and (c) make "not printable in the recap PDF" one of the conditions that triggers INV-113's pinned name question at graduation, where declining still costs nothing (INV-048). The font-safety inventory MUST cover names, not only punctuation and symbols. (Enforces INV-143, whose inventory covered what deliverables carry *except* the most certain thing they carry: a Bootcamper named 李明 had `??` printed on their certificate, silently, at exit 0 — found by the 2026-07-28 deep-dive audit. Complements INV-113/INV-134; `tests/test_recap_pdf_font_safety.py` enforces it and MUST pass.) (Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-28`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: A generator MUST NOT reduce any character of a Bootcamper-authored value to `?`, and this MUST hold for the Bootcamper's **name** specifically — the string INV-134 detects from `git config user.name` and the Certificate of Completion prints largest.

invariants.statement: Where an MCP tool's response carries **both** a payload field and metadata describing that payload's size or completeness, a payload that contradicts its own metadata MUST be treated as a **failed retrieval**, never as a real empty result: concretely, `find_examples` file retrieval (`repo` + `file_path`) returning an empty `content` alongside a non-zero `content_length` means the retrieval failed, and `truncated: false` MUST NOT be read as confirming completeness. The guide MUST fall back to the response's own documented access path (fetch `raw_url`, or clone per `access_steps`) and MUST NOT tell the Bootcamper an example file is empty, or silently skip the example, on that basis. An undeclared parameter MUST NOT be adopted as the remedy even when the response's own prose advertises one — only parameters the live schema declares may be passed (INV-136). This does **not** conflict with INV-149: an empty result with *no* contradicting metadata (an empty `response_schemas` `data` array) is coverage, not failure — it is the contradiction that signals the defect. Verified 2026-07-28 against server 1.32.1. (⚠️ **Premise corrected 2026-08-11 against server 1.32.8; every MUST above is unchanged and still binding.** The `find_examples` file-retrieval payload no longer contradicts its metadata — it **declares** the omission: the empty `content` now arrives with **`content_elided: true`** and an ordered `access_steps` array (fetch `raw_url` → `git clone` → an `inline` step that only clients forwarding undeclared arguments can use). So that response is a deliberate elision, not a failed retrieval, and the concrete example above should be read as what 1.32.1 returned rather than as the current test. Proved rather than inferred: a ~20 KB file and a ~800-byte file elide identically, with and without `max_lines`, so it is unconditional and no smaller request returns the body; search mode still returns real `code_snippet` content. The same elision now applies to **`generate_scaffold`**, whose `snippets[]` carry `raw_url`, `size_bytes` and `line_count` and no inline code — so this invariant's scope is the elision shape wherever it appears, not `find_examples` alone. The undeclared-`inline` prohibition is untouched and is now stated by the server itself: *"Clients that validate arguments against the declared schema cannot use this step; prefer fetching raw_url or cloning."* What this changes is the **reason** the guidance holds, not the guidance: fall back to `raw_url`/clone, never tell the Bootcamper an example file is empty, never adopt an undeclared parameter. Source: `find-examples-elision-is-by-design-not-a-failed-retrieval`.) (Source: `find-examples-file-retrieval-returns-empty-content`, 2026-07-28.)

A relative asset reference inside a generated deliverable's source document (e.g. a recap `![alt](path)`) MUST be resolved against **that document's own directory**, never against the process working directory. The path that is correct for reading the source in a Markdown renderer MUST also be correct for rendering it, so an author following the instruction cannot produce a lossy artifact, and no step may require a `cd` to make assets resolve. (Before this, `generate_recap_pdf.py` resolved against `Path.cwd()` while graduation ran it from the project root, so document-relative screenshot paths silently resolved to nothing and no path satisfied both the Markdown recap and the PDF. Source: `recap-pdf-images-resolve-against-recap-directory`, 2026-07-28.) ⚠️ **Forward pointer, 2026-08-14 — nothing here is superseded.** This invariant states one instance of a general rule now registered as **INV-242**: prose instructing the guide to author content a bundled script must parse states the shape that script accepts. The path is that shape's *value*; INV-242 governs the shape itself, and the same instruction was found silently broken a second way — screenshots written as `- ![…](…)` bullets, which the image detector did not match. Cite INV-242 for the general statement and this one for the path.
invariants.summary: A relative asset reference inside a generated deliverable's source document (e.g.

invariants.statement: A generator that drops a referenced asset from a deliverable MUST report each drop on stderr, distinguishing "not found" from "found but unusable", and MUST report an embedded-of-referenced count alongside any content-retention figure. A character-retention figure structurally cannot see a missing image — the characters do render — so retention alone MUST NOT be presented as evidence of a complete artifact: a recap that lost all six of the Bootcamper's screenshots reported `rendered 46707 of 46973 source characters (99%)` and exit 0, and the only clue was an implausibly small file. The drop itself stays non-fatal (INV-048); only silence is forbidden. Where a renderer embeds no assets by design (the stdlib fallback), the count MUST say so rather than reading as a lookup failure. (Extends INV-110/INV-111 from characters to embedded assets. Source: `recap-pdf-images-resolve-against-recap-directory`, 2026-07-28.) (⚠️ **Constrained by INV-193 — cross-referenced 2026-07-31, no meaning change.** The embedded-of-referenced count required here is a **loss** signal: it answers *"did anything this document referenced fail to embed?"*. It MUST NOT be presented as evidence that the artifact is **complete**, because its denominator is read from the document being rendered and therefore cannot see a captured view the document never referenced — a recap embedding four of six captured tabs reports `embedded 4 of 4 images`. A completeness claim MUST take its denominator from outside the artifact (INV-193), and where no external count is available the coverage check MUST report itself skipped rather than passed (INV-163). Both counts are required and neither substitutes for the other; stated here because the any-language contract is built from these invariants and not from the Python reference's comments.)
invariants.summary: A generator that drops a referenced asset from a deliverable MUST report each drop on stderr, distinguishing "not found" from "found but unusable", and MUST report an embedded-of-referenced count alongside any content-retention figure.

invariants.statement: A verification check that cannot run because its tool is absent MUST be recorded as skipped, naming the check, and any completion or closing message MUST state which verification steps did not run; an artifact MUST NOT be described as verified for a check that did not execute. Where a check's tool is not present on every supported platform — poppler (`pdftoppm` / `pdftotext` / `pdfimages` / `pdfinfo`) is absent by default on **both Windows and macOS**, so the page raster and the honest image count are exactly the checks those runs lose — the guidance MUST offer a route needing no new dependency, since INV-129 forbids installing one to satisfy a check. (⚠️ **Platform example corrected 2026-07-31.** As first recorded this named Windows alone, because "poppler is standard on Linux and macOS" is the habitual pairing for Unix-like tooling. It is wrong: poppler is a Linux distribution package, not a macOS system component, and a macOS 26.5.2 machine **with Homebrew in active use** had all four binaries absent. Nothing could have caught it — no test can check what is installed on a platform the suite is not running on, and this repo's CI runs on Linux, where the claim happens to hold. The MUST above is unchanged; only the example was wrong.) Concretely for the recap PDF: the generator's own embedded-image count, then Pillow (already present via `fpdf2` in the project-local venv of INV-066), before `pdfimages -list`, and the `/Subtype /Image` grep last and labeled as overcounting. A skipped check never blocks (INV-048, INV-052/INV-066) and this stays agent-side apparatus, not Bootcamper-facing output (INV-012). (Extends INV-129 from performing verification to reporting its coverage: a keepsake whose layout nobody could inspect is acceptable, one described as verified when its layout was never inspected is not. Source: `pdf-layout-verification-without-poppler`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: A verification check that cannot run because its tool is absent MUST be recorded as skipped, naming the check, and any completion or closing message MUST state which verification steps did not run; an artifact MUST NOT be described as verified for a check that did not execute.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: A name search the Bootcamp performs or generates MUST NOT use `NAME_FULL` alone: it MUST also try `NAME_ORG`, because per the Senzing Entity Specification (Name > Feature: NAME) `NAME_ORG` is the organization name attribute while `NAME_FULL` is the single-field attribute for a name whose type is unknown — so an organization name sent as `NAME_FULL` matches nothing **and raises no error**. The response MUST report which attributes were tried, and a zero-result search MUST be rendered as "nothing matched the attributes tried", never as absence from the data (INV-115). This binds a visualization or query program in **any** language (INV-090/INV-124), not only the bundled Python reference: the defect reached a generated query program precisely because it lived in the reference implementation and in no written rule. Observed on a half-organization dataset, where search silently failed for about half the population. (Source: `organization-search-requires-name-org`, 2026-07-28.) (⚠️ **See also INV-183, 2026-08-11.** It generalizes the *lesson* of this invariant — a rule reachable only through a reference implementation does not reach generated code — into a standing requirement that every authoring step names the rules governing its artifact. The attribute rule stated here is **not** superseded and binds unchanged; INV-183 governs where it must appear.)

An example, hint, or suggested query offered to the Bootcamper MUST be verified by **actually running it** and MUST return at least one result; deriving it from real loaded data is NOT verification. One that returns nothing MUST be dropped with a reported reason (stderr at build time, `console.warn` in a live page), never shipped as a dead control — a hint that finds nothing is worse than no hint, and it also silently misattributes a query defect to the Bootcamper's data. Observed: every Search / Probe chip named after an organization was a real merged entity and still returned nothing, because search tried `NAME_FULL` only (INV-164). (Enforces the "pre-verified" claim the visualization contract already made. Source: `organization-search-requires-name-org`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: An example, hint, or suggested query offered to the Bootcamper MUST be verified by **actually running it** and MUST return at least one result; deriving it from real loaded data is NOT verification.

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: Every file the Bootcamp writes MUST be byte-correct UTF-8 with no BOM, and generated files MUST be written through Python or the agent's file tools rather than PowerShell redirection. On PowerShell 5.1 `-Encoding utf8` writes a BOM and `Get-Content` without `-Encoding` decodes as the system ANSI codepage, and both corruptions are invisible to every obvious check — a BOM makes only record 1 of a JSONL fail (reading as one bad source record rather than an encoding fault), and a double-encoded document is valid UTF-8 containing no U+FFFD, merely wrong. Windows-1252 mojibake MUST therefore be detected and reported over `docs/*.md` before the recap renders, and **reported rather than silently repaired**, since a repair is a content change and the normalizer's contract is that it changes formatting only (INV-110). (Source: `windows-powershell-encoding-and-syntax`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: Every file the Bootcamp writes MUST be byte-correct UTF-8 with no BOM, and generated files MUST be written through Python or the agent's file tools rather than PowerShell redirection.

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: Where the SBCP offers a PowerShell counterpart to a shell command, that counterpart MUST use PowerShell syntax and MUST NOT carry bash-shaped constructs: no `&&`/`||` chaining (use `A; if ($?) { B }`), no `if` used as an expression, no ternary or null-coalescing, no heredocs, and no inline `python -c`. Multi-line or quote-heavy code MUST be placed in a script file under `src/` (INV-018) and run as a file. Each of these is a *parser* error on Windows PowerShell 5.1 — the default `powershell.exe` on Windows 11, whose limits the plugin's guidance MUST assume unless it has verified `pwsh` 7+ — so the message points at syntax rather than at the real cause, which is a command written for another shell. (`tests/test_windows_powershell_guidance.py` sweeps every PowerShell block for `&&`/`||` and MUST pass.) (Source: `windows-powershell-encoding-and-syntax`, 2026-07-28.)

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: A helper that discovers an external executable MUST search each supported platform's conventional install locations, not only `PATH` plus one platform's absolute paths, and MUST expand those locations from the environment rather than hard-coding a drive letter or a localizable directory name. It MUST NOT report a capability as absent when it is present, and when it does report one absent it MUST name the locations searched — being told to install software one already has is worse than "not found", because it sends the reader to fix the wrong thing. A run where the executable was **found** but the operation still produced nothing MUST be reported distinctly from one where nothing was found (extending INV-122's reason-distinguishing rule to a third case). Where the capability is genuinely missing the helper still degrades per its own contract and MUST NOT install anything to satisfy itself (INV-122, INV-129). Observed: Windows places neither Chrome nor Edge on `PATH`, so a Windows 11 workstation carrying both was told no screenshot capability was available and lost every recap screenshot, while `C:\Program Files\...` was never examined. (Source: `windows-headless-browser-discovery-for-screenshots`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: A helper that discovers an external executable MUST search each supported platform's conventional install locations, not only `PATH` plus one platform's absolute paths, and MUST expand those locations from the environment rather than hard-coding a drive letter or a localizable directory name.

invariants.statement: A single observation of SDK behavior MUST NOT be generalized into an absolute about a *method*. Where behavior varies with flags, version, or binding, the guidance MUST record what was observed together with the flag set, SDK version and binding it was observed under, and MUST route the reader through a per-installation check (dump one row and read it) rather than asserting the outcome. Stating an over-generalized absolute is worse than stating nothing: it teaches that a correct approach is broken, and a reader who meets a contradicting MCP source has no way to adjudicate without dumping a row themselves. Where an MCP tool documents the behavior, that citation governs and MUST be given (INV-080); the dumped row remains the authority for what a given installation actually returns (INV-115/INV-149). Observed twice: `SZ_EXPORT_ALL_FLAGS` was shipped as "does not exist" and needed a five-place retraction (INV-132), and phase D shipped "do not expect `RELATED_ENTITIES` from `export_json_entity_report`" — false under `SZ_EXPORT_DEFAULT_FLAGS`, and contradicted by `reporting_guide(topic='evaluation')`. (Source: `export-related-entities-is-flag-conditional`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: A single observation of SDK behavior MUST NOT be generalized into an absolute about a *method*.

invariants.statement: A value the Bootcamper was **asked for** MUST outrank any value auto-detected before the question was asked, and MUST be persisted everywhere the artifact is generated from. A generator choosing between two sources for the same field MUST prefer the answer and MUST report on stderr when the two disagree, naming both values and the one it used (INV-111). Recording an answer in one place while the generator reads another is indistinguishable from never having asked: graduation's pre-check rejected the auto-detected handle `docktermj`, asked the pinned certificate-name question, recorded the reply as `name` in `config/bootcamp_preferences.yaml` — and the certificate still printed `docktermj`, because the generator read the recap's `**Bootcamper:**` line written at the start of the run, at exit 0 with 99% content retention and no warning (INV-065/INV-113). Retention cannot catch this class: the wrong value does render, so nothing is missing (INV-110 measures loss, not correctness). (Source: `certificate-name-must-reach-the-generator`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: A value the Bootcamper was **asked for** MUST outrank any value auto-detected before the question was asked, and MUST be persisted everywhere the artifact is generated from.

invariants.statement: Apparatus that captures a bootcamper-facing artifact MUST NOT perturb what it is capturing. A view-switching function MUST be idempotent — invoked for the view already shown, it MUST return without redrawing — because a redraw restarts any animated layout and the capture then records an unsettled intermediate state as if it were the result. This binds the app in whichever language it is generated (INV-090/INV-124) rather than any one capture caller, since every capture route (an injected `activate('<tab>')`, `?tab=<id>` deep-linking) and a plain user click all reach the same function; a guard placed in one caller leaves the others defective. Where content animates to its final position, the capture MUST also allow it longer to settle than static content, and that allowance MUST be documented as settle time rather than a timeout. Observed: re-activating the already-active Entity Graph restarted its force simulation mid-capture and produced a valid 47 KB PNG (against ~227 KB) of every node collapsed in a corner, at exit 0, which then reached the recap under a caption describing a graph the image did not show (INV-123). (Source: `default-tab-capture-without-injection`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: Apparatus that captures a bootcamper-facing artifact MUST NOT perturb what it is capturing.

invariants.statement: A retained artifact MUST NOT hardcode a fact about the environment that produced it, nor assert an identity for the Bootcamper's data that the caller did not supply. A port MUST be derived from the parsed value actually in use, and dataset wording MUST come from the caller with a neutral default ("the loaded data") — never a guess such as "this Truth Set", since one code path serves the Senzing Truth Set in its own module and the Bootcamper's own data in Query, Visualize and Discover. Such text ships permanently into `docs/visualizations/*.html`, so a wrong claim there is unfalsifiable to the reader and outlives the run: a Module 7 snapshot on a non-default port told its reader to open a port nothing was listening on **and** mislabeled their data as a Senzing demo set. A caller-supplied label reaching rendered HTML MUST be escaped for that context (INV-106). (Source: `snapshot-port-and-dataset-wording`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: A retained artifact MUST NOT hardcode a fact about the environment that produced it, nor assert an identity for the Bootcamper's data that the caller did not supply.

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: Where a validation gate **cannot represent** a legitimate input, its finding MUST NOT be treated as evidence about the data, MUST NOT block the flow (INV-048), and MUST NOT be resolved by altering the data to satisfy the gate. The guidance MUST name the limitation with its provenance, state the exemption path (verify faithfulness against the authority for the artifact — for mapped output, the Senzing Entity Specification via MCP — record the reason, proceed), and MUST NOT ship a forked copy of an MCP-delivered validator, since a fork masks the upstream fix (INV-080). Observed: `sz_verbatim_check.py` harvests its allowed set from string values only (`isinstance(obj, str)`) and offers a key-based waiver alone (`EXEMPT_KEYS = {"DATA_SOURCE", "RECORD_ID"}` plus any attribute ending `_TYPE`), so a numeric source value is reported as a violation whichever way it is emitted — a gate that is unsatisfiable rather than strict, which fired on all 53,321 relationship rows of a correct mapping, and whose obvious workaround distorts the data without even passing. (Second instance of this shape; the first was an MCP-delivered analyzer reporting false errors on a legacy-but-valid format — `analyzer-legacy-sublist-format-false-errors`.) (Source: `verbatim-check-numeric-source-values`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: Where a validation gate **cannot represent** a legitimate input, its finding MUST NOT be treated as evidence about the data, MUST NOT block the flow (INV-048), and MUST NOT be resolved by altering the data to satisfy the gate.

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: A completeness, coverage or quality metric MUST NOT count against a record a field that cannot apply to it. Measure per record against the fields applicable to that record's kind — for Senzing data, its `RECORD_TYPE` — and aggregate those per-record results; never average one field's coverage across a whole source of mixed kinds. Applicability MUST be derived from the authority for the data (for mapped output, the Senzing Entity Specification via MCP, which marks type in its feature descriptions and section headings — `DOB` is "Person date of birth", `REGISTRATION_DATE` sits under "(organizations)") rather than from a list hardcoded in the plugin (INV-080), and fields that apply to every kind (`ADDRESS`, `PHONE`, `EMAIL`, identifiers) MUST NOT be excluded. Where a record's kind is unknown — `RECORD_TYPE` is "Recommended", not required — score it against kind-independent fields and report how many records were scored that way. This class of error fails toward false alarm: a sanctions list with NAME and ADDRESS on 100% of records scored 69% and was routed to "recommend fixing before mapping" because person-only features were averaged across a source that was 65% organizations; per-type rescoring gave 97%. (Extends INV-128's presence test from what counts as a present *value* to what belongs in the *denominator*. Source: `quality-score-per-record-type`, 2026-07-28.)
invariants.summary: A completeness, coverage or quality metric MUST NOT count against a record a field that cannot apply to it.

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: Any script the SBCP tells the Bootcamper to `source` MUST resolve its own location in the platform's **default** shell rather than assuming bash, MUST verify the path it computed before exporting anything derived from it, and on failure MUST `return` — never `exit` or `set -e`, which kill or contaminate the Bootcamper's own shell — with a message naming the resolved path (INV-111). `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is bash-only and expands to **empty** under zsh, macOS's default shell and therefore the shell a Bootcamper following `source src/scripts/senzing-env.sh` is actually in, so the project root resolves to the wrong directory and the script carries on: every export is wrong and the error surfaces far from its cause. A value derived from an unverified root MUST NOT be exported, and an **empty** value MUST NOT be exported in place of no value — Senzing's own official snippets guard initialization with `settings == null`, testing for *unset* and not empty (`search_docs`, server 1.32.1, 2026-07-28), so an empty export defeats the SDK's own check and fails deeper. Where the plugin ships the idiom it MUST state it once and link to it, and the shipped snippet MUST be executed by a test rather than only asserted present. (Extends INV-166/INV-167 from Windows/PowerShell to the macOS/zsh half of the same class: a supported platform's default shell whose semantics went undocumented. Source: `env-script-must-be-shell-portable`, 2026-07-28.)

Every End-of-Module Summary block MUST be authored in its required **shape**, not merely carry its label: `**What you accomplished:**` and `**Files produced:**` are lists — the label on its own line, then one bullet per accomplishment and one bullet per file with a short "— what it is" gloss — while `**Why it matters:**` is prose that stays inline after its label. The recap PDF renders bullets as bullets and inline text as one wrapped paragraph, so a list authored inline (most often a comma-joined run of paths) reaches the keepsake as a paragraph and cannot be recovered downstream; `--check` validates the label, never the shape, so both shapes pass every existing gate. This binds what the plugin **authors** — `module-completion.md`'s template, graduation's Step 1a backfill, and the shipped `docs/examples/bootcamp_recap.example.md` — and MUST NOT be enforced on **parsing**: existing recaps carry the inline shape and INV-103's presence check is deliberately shape-independent. (Extends INV-103 from which blocks are present to how they are written. Source: `recap-summary-blocks-authored-as-bullets`, 2026-07-29.)

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: When a per-source workflow run writes fixed, non-source-qualified filenames into a workspace directory **shared across sources**, every such artifact MUST be relocated to its durable home under a **source-qualified** name before the next source's run begins, and any guidance naming that shared workspace MUST state the qualifier for every fixed filename the workspace receives. `mapping_workflow` writes `profile_report.md`, `schema_hints.md` and `JOURNAL.md` into the single `workspace_dir` under fixed names, with `JOURNAL.md` explicitly append-only (`mapping_workflow(action='start')`, server 1.32.2, verified 2026-07-29; **re-confirmed unchanged on server 1.32.9, 2026-08-13** — step 1 still writes exactly those three fixed names into `workspace_dir` and still calls `JOURNAL.md` "APPEND-ONLY … NEVER rewrite the whole file") — so relocating them unqualified makes each source overwrite, or append onto, the previous source's durable record, silently and with no error. Use the `{source_name}_` form already required for `docs/mapping/{source_name}_mapper.md`. (Source: `module-05-shared-workspace-transient-filename-collision`, 2026-07-29.) (⚠️ **Premise corrected 2026-08-23. Clarified 2026-08-23, no meaning change — the RULE is unchanged and still binding.** The three-fixed-names premise holds only for a **single-file** `start`. On server **1.33.0, 2026-08-23** a multi-file `mapping_workflow(action='start')` emits one profiler invocation per input, each writing `<workspace_dir>/profile_report_<stem>.md` — so the workspace receives `profile_report_crm.md` and `profile_report_orders.md`, neither of which the sentence above names. The rule was always stated in the general — *every* such artifact, *every* fixed filename the workspace receives — so it already binds those files; what was narrower than reality was the illustrative list, and a reader matching the literal `profile_report.md` would leave a suffixed report in the shared workspace and reproduce exactly the overwrite this invariant prevents. Read the rule as binding **every profile report the workspace receives**, whatever the server named it. Enforced at both relocation sites in `module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase2-data-mapping.md` and by `tests/test_profile_report_relocation_covers_both_filenames.py`. Source: `profile-report-filename-is-conditional-on-file-count`, 2026-08-23.)

A bundled generator that drops a character it cannot encode MUST report the loss on **stderr**, once per run, naming how many distinct characters and passages were affected, identifying the characters by **Unicode name** (never by echoing the character itself), and quoting one locating excerpt with non-ASCII backslash-escaped — while still writing the artifact and exiting 0. The report MUST be pure ASCII, because a legacy Windows code page cannot display the very characters that were dropped and would corrupt the warning into the mojibake it exists to report. A retention or content-retained percentage MUST NOT be treated as covering this class: retention is measured over parsed *source* characters, before sanitization runs at render time, so a Cyrillic organization name vanished at "content retained: 96%", exit 0. Reporting MUST be limited to characters that render as **nothing**; a deliberate readable approximation (a stripped combining mark leaving its base letter, or a mapped ASCII equivalent) MUST NOT be reported, or ordinary accented names bury the real losses. (Extends INV-143 from *how* a generator may drop to *that it must say so*. Source: `generators-warn-on-dropped-unencodable-characters`, 2026-07-29.)

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: Before writing code that reads a field from an SDK response, the guide MUST confirm the flag that populates **that field** is present in the flag composite actually in force, reading its `composite_members` — not merely that the field name is correct. A method's own named default composite is **not** `SZ_ENTITY_DEFAULT_FLAGS` and may omit sub-flags that one carries: `SZ_SEARCH_BY_ATTRIBUTES_ALL` and `SZ_FIND_NETWORK_DEFAULT_FLAGS` both carry `SZ_ENTITY_INCLUDE_RECORD_SUMMARY` and omit `SZ_ENTITY_INCLUDE_RECORD_DATA`, and both are the **signature defaults**, so passing no `flags` argument hits this too (server 1.32.2, verified 2026-07-29). A blank field therefore has **three** causes, not two, and the guide MUST NOT stop at the first: a wrong field name, **a correct field name the flags in force do not populate**, or genuinely absent data. Where `response_schemas` confirms the path and a sibling field from the same object reads fine, the flags MUST be suspected before the data, and the fix is to OR in the missing sub-flag — never to switch fields or re-verify a name already known correct. (Extends INV-115, whose two-cause wording this corrects. Source: `method-default-flags-omit-record-data`, 2026-07-29.)
invariants.summary: Before writing code that reads a field from an SDK response, the guide MUST confirm the flag that populates **that field** is present in the flag composite actually in force, reading its `composite_members` — not merely that the field name is correct.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: Code that walks a source's raw or mapped file rows to associate them with resolved entities MUST deduplicate by `(data_source, record_id)` before counting or grouping. A Senzing record's identity is that pair, and re-sending it **replaces** the record rather than adding another (`search_docs`, "Data Source Records (DSRs) Explained"; `get_sdk_reference(topic='parameters', filter='add_record')`; server 1.32.2, verified 2026-07-29) — so *n* rows sharing a key are **one** record, and a mapped file may legitimately hold more rows than distinct keys. Senzing's resolved view, never the file, is the authority on how many records an entity has: a surprising per-record count MUST be cross-checked against it before being reported as a finding. Counting rows once inflated two entities to 23 and 15 records against 2 real ones each, falsely routing both to over-matching review. (Source: `query-programs-dedupe-source-rows-by-record-key`, 2026-07-29.)
invariants.summary: Code that walks a source's raw or mapped file rows to associate them with resolved entities MUST deduplicate by `(data_source, record_id)` before counting or grouping.

invariants.statement: When the MCP server changes behavior the plugin documents, every place the plugin states the superseded behavior MUST be corrected to the current behavior — including test assertions and docstrings that pin it — and MUST NOT be left version-conditioned to an older server. The plugin pins no MCP **server** version (every `version` argument is the Senzing SDK version), so a Bootcamper always reaches the deployed server and text describing an earlier one actively misleads: the retired numeric verbatim-check claim told them to record an exemption for a gate that had become green. A superseded claim MUST be recorded by appending to its originating spec, never by editing that spec's text, and a test that pinned it MUST be repointed to what survives — the rule or discipline — with a docstring stating what changed and when. (Source: `verbatim-check-numeric-source-values` superseded 2026-07-29.)
invariants.summary: When the MCP server changes behavior the plugin documents, every place the plugin states the superseded behavior MUST be corrected to the current behavior — including test assertions and docstrings that pin it — and MUST NOT be left version-conditioned to an older server.

invariants.statement: A spec MUST NOT be recorded as implemented in `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` until **each** of its `## Acceptance criteria` has been checked individually with its evidence named (a `file:line`, a test, or a command run). A criterion that cannot be proven MUST be recorded as a deviation or as not-runtime-verified — never ticked — and a criterion naming a file, a module, or a **second consumer** MUST be verified by opening that file, not against the change the implementer remembers making. The ledger heading is the only completion signal the repo has and nothing downstream re-checks it: `relocate-integration-deployment-questions-to-module1` was recorded done with graduation never reading the answers its criterion named (INV-097, seven weeks), and `defer-commonmark-to-graduation` with the `production/*.md` half of its pass never built (INV-060, six weeks) — both invisible because neither invariant is cited by any test. (Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-29-minor-fixes`, 2026-07-29.)
invariants.summary: A spec MUST NOT be recorded as implemented in `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` until **each** of its `## Acceptance criteria` has been checked individually with its evidence named (a `file:line`, a test, or a command run).

invariants.statement: A step that instructs the guide to generate a bootcamper-facing artifact MUST, **at that step**, name every rule governing how the artifact is produced — or cite the file that states it — and MUST NOT rely on a rule stated only elsewhere. The step is the only text the guide is certainly reading when it authors the artifact, so a binding rule one file away is unreachable in practice. For a generated page or document that is currently: the shared brand tokens and offline rendering (INV-081/INV-091), escaping of every data-sourced string for the context it lands in (INV-106), verification of the rendered artifact rather than the exit status (INV-129), and its required location (INV-070). The rule MUST be **named and linked, never restated or forked** at the step (INV-080's no-fork discipline), so one statement of record stays authoritative. Observed: Module 5's two `docs/visualizations/` pages were instructed in a single sentence, with the brand MUST reachable only through a "should … where appropriate" restatement and the escaping rule only from another module's contract — so a CDN chart library, an unbranded page, and unescaped bootcamper data were all conforming readings. (Generalizes INV-164 from a reference implementation to any authoring instruction; `tests/test_generated_html_deliverables.py` enforces it for generated HTML, and the invariant is deliberately broader than that test since the next such artifact may not be HTML.) (Source: `module5-quality-pages-are-branded-visual-deliverables`, 2026-07-30.)
invariants.summary: A step that instructs the guide to generate a bootcamper-facing artifact MUST, **at that step**, name every rule governing how the artifact is produced — or cite the file that states it — and MUST NOT rely on a rule stated only elsewhere.

invariants.statement: Every shipped generator that inlines a fallback copy of the brand palette MUST keep that copy equal to the values `brand_tokens.py` derives, MUST hold it in a single named constant rather than repeating the literals per code path, and MUST have that equality asserted by `tests/test_brand_sync.py`. INV-107 named two generators; the property belongs to the *pattern*, and the third (`generate_discoveries_pdf.py`) drifted out of scope unnoticed while its own comment claimed a test asserted it. (Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-30`, 2026-07-30.)
invariants.summary: Every shipped generator that inlines a fallback copy of the brand palette MUST keep that copy equal to the values `brand_tokens.py` derives, MUST hold it in a single named constant rather than repeating the literals per code path, and MUST have that equality asserted by `tests/test_brand_sync.py`.

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: Every command the SBCP tells the guide to run against a **bundled** script MUST resolve that script inside the plugin — `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<name>.py`, with the documented skill-relative fallback (`<this-skill-dir>/../../scripts/<name>.py`) — and MUST NOT name it by a bare project-relative path. The command runs in the Bootcamper's project while the script ships in the plugin, and the project layout (INV-050) has no top-level `scripts/`; its own utilities live under `src/scripts/`. `python3 scripts/generate_discoveries_pdf.py` therefore exits 2 with `can't open file` from any project root — and because it was the sole invocation of that generator, and its step is explicitly "report exactly what failed and continue", the realistic outcome was the always-produced data-discoveries deliverable being reported missing rather than produced. Prose-only review cannot catch this class: the line is valid shell and wrong only relative to a working directory no reader is holding. (`tests/test_bundled_script_and_production_paths.py` sweeps every invocation and MUST pass.) (Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-30b`, 2026-07-30.)

Where a generated deliverable copies code **verbatim**, every data or asset tree that code reads MUST be copied to the same path **relative to the project root**, and the code MUST NOT be rewritten to match a flattened destination. Graduation copied `src/load/**` unchanged to `production/src/load/` while flattening `data/senzing-ready/**` to `production/data/`, so the handover project's loader pointed at a directory that did not exist — invisible to every check, because both halves of the copy succeeded. Rewriting the path instead is forbidden for the same reason it is tempting: the code is the Bootcamper's, and a path edited by graduation is a change they never saw made. (Upholds INV-084 across the `production/` boundary. Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-30b`, 2026-07-30.)
invariants.summary: Where a generated deliverable copies code **verbatim**, every data or asset tree that code reads MUST be copied to the same path **relative to the project root**, and the code MUST NOT be rewritten to match a flattened destination.

invariants.statement: An input the graduation handover deliberately does **not** copy MUST be named in the handover — in `production/GRADUATION_REPORT.md`'s files-excluded table and in `production/README.md`'s Configuration section — saying where the reader must supply it. `data/raw/` is excluded by design (raw source data is the Bootcamper's to place), but a CORD fast-pathed source loads straight from it with no mapping (INV-040/INV-041), so its loader arrives in `production/` with nothing to read. An excluded input the handover never mentions is indistinguishable from a broken project, and the reader has no way to tell which they are looking at. (Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-30b`, 2026-07-30.)
invariants.summary: An input the graduation handover deliberately does **not** copy MUST be named in the handover — in `production/GRADUATION_REPORT.md`'s files-excluded table and in `production/README.md`'s Configuration section — saying where the reader must supply it.

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: A user-visible string a shipped script **emits** — `--help` text, an error message, any list built at runtime from a data structure — is bound by the same content invariants as the plugin's prose, and conformance MUST be verified by **executing** the script, never by reading the source that produces the string. A guard that scans source cannot see an f-string's output, and the framing that makes a source construct correct does not travel with the value it interpolates: `capture_screenshots.py` kept `network` and `merges` in `TABS` under an explicit "⛔ RESERVED" comment — correct, and necessary so an eight-tab snapshot keeps its slugs — while `--help` and the unknown-id error interpolated the whole dict and presented eight capturable tabs for an app INV-155 fixes at six. A reserved value the script still accepts MUST be reported as retired when it is used, since accepting it silently is what keeps a stale list believed. (Extends INV-155's tab-set conformance from prose and docstrings to emitted strings; `tests/test_tab_set_is_singular.py` runs `--help` and the error path.) (Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-30b`, 2026-07-30.)

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: Install and setup instructions MUST cover every platform INV-001 supports, or explicitly route an uncovered platform to the interface that does serve it. A step headed "on macOS or Linux" with no Windows line and no redirect reads as the complete set, so a Windows reader concludes the route does not exist rather than that it went unwritten — and the two facts are indistinguishable from the page. Where a command differs per platform it MUST be given per platform, verified against the vendor's own current documentation rather than recalled (the Claude Code CLI installs with `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash` on macOS/Linux/WSL and `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` in Windows PowerShell — verified 2026-07-30 against code.claude.com/docs/en/setup), and a PowerShell counterpart still obeys INV-167. (Source: `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-30b`, 2026-07-30.)
invariants.summary: Install and setup instructions MUST cover every platform INV-001 supports, or explicitly route an uncovered platform to the interface that does serve it.

invariants.statement: Where a lookup tries a **list** of candidates in order — name attributes, encodings, endpoints, paths — an attempt that **fails** MUST be recorded and retried past, never treated as the end of the list. An error is reported only after every candidate has been attempted and none produced a result, and the report MUST name which candidates were tried and which failed; a result found by a later candidate stands, and a failure behind it is not an error. A guard phrased as "nothing has matched **yet**" is not a guard for "there is nothing **left to try**" — the two coincide only on the final candidate, so the defect hides on exactly the first one. Observed in the bundled visualization server, where `if not items: return {…}` meant any engine error searching `NAME_FULL` returned before `NAME_ORG` was ever called, silently reinstating the INV-164 defect on the error path with a message attached naming the attribute that could not have matched an organization anyway. This binds a query or visualization program in **any** language (INV-090/INV-124), not only the bundled Python reference. (Hardens INV-164 on the error path; complements INV-115.) (Source: `search-attribute-fallback-survives-a-failed-attempt`, 2026-07-30.)
invariants.summary: Where a lookup tries a **list** of candidates in order — name attributes, encodings, endpoints, paths — an attempt that **fails** MUST be recorded and retried past, never treated as the end of the list.

invariants.statement: A dated provenance stamp MUST NOT be advanced for a claim that was not re-verified in that pass, and a refresh MUST target the specific provenance it re-checked rather than every date in the sentence. A line commonly carries two: an MCP stamp the sweep can re-ask, and a live-engine observation it structurally cannot (`visualization-api-reference.md` cites both — "re-verified on MCP server 1.32.2, 2026-07-30 — and corroborated by a dump on SDK 4.3.3, 2026-07-28"). Advancing the second asserts a check that never ran, and it is invisible afterwards because a fresh date is exactly what a verified claim looks like. Where a claim cannot be re-checked in the current environment its stamp MUST be left as written and the gap recorded as skipped (INV-163), never closed by restamping. (Observed 2026-07-30: a line-targeted stamp refresh bumped a live-dump date to a day no dump was run; caught by `tests/test_partial_row_and_schema_coverage.py`. Hardens INV-080.) (Source: `refresh-reverified-provenance-stamps`, 2026-07-30.)
invariants.summary: A dated provenance stamp MUST NOT be advanced for a claim that was not re-verified in that pass, and a refresh MUST target the specific provenance it re-checked rather than every date in the sentence.

invariants.statement: A parameter an MCP tool's schema marks **optional** may still be mandatory to its *answer*, and a response that asks for one is a **gate, not a result**. Where a tool replies with a `needs_input` decision tree — or any response whose payload sections come back empty while it names a parameter it wants — the guide MUST re-call with that parameter satisfied, MUST NOT parse the gate as content, and MUST NOT conclude from it that a topic has no guidance. Every documented call in the plugin MUST pass the gating parameter, and where a tool gates only on *some* inputs the guidance MUST say which, since a caller who succeeds on the ungated ones has no reason to suspect the rest. Concretely on server 1.32.2 (2026-07-30): `reporting_guide` returns a `needs_input` gate on `language` for `topic='evaluation'` and `topic='graph'`, and on `language` then `scale` for `topic='data_mart'`, while `topic='quality'` returns its content without one — six shipped sites omitted `language`, including a step that cited the 4-Point ER Evaluation Framework as its reason for the call, which is exactly what the gated response withholds. This class is invisible to INV-136, which governs only what the *schema* declares required: a call can satisfy the schema completely, return HTTP 200, and carry a plausible partial payload while the substance is absent. That partial population is the hazard — an empty response reads as failure, whereas a gate carrying a few `anti_patterns` reads as an answer (the INV-115 half-populated-row trap, applied to a tool response rather than a record). (Extends INV-136 from declared requirements to runtime ones; complements INV-115 and INV-125.) (Source: `reporting-guide-topics-gate-on-language`, 2026-07-30.)
invariants.summary: A parameter an MCP tool's schema marks **optional** may still be mandatory to its *answer*, and a response that asks for one is a **gate, not a result**.

invariants.statement: A count or percentage presented as evidence of **completeness** MUST derive its denominator from outside the artifact it measures. A self-derived figure MUST state what it cannot detect and MUST NOT be cited as proof of completeness. Observed: `generate_recap_pdf.py`'s `embedded N of M images` took `M` from the count of `![](…)` links in the very recap it was rendering, so a recap that embedded only four of six captured tabs reported `embedded 4 of 4 images` — a perfect score against an incomplete set, structurally incapable of detecting the incompleteness it appears to measure. In the reporting session the assistant cited `embedded 12 of 12` to a Bootcamper as proof the screenshots were complete *while being asked exactly that question*; it was right by luck of the input, not by measurement. That is worse than having no metric, because it is the number a reader naturally reaches for. The fix is an external denominator — here `capture_screenshots.py`'s `<name>-tabs.json` manifest, the only count in the chain not read from the recap — and where none is available the check MUST report itself **skipped** rather than passed (INV-163). Distinct from INV-110, which requires that loss be made visible but says nothing about where a denominator comes from: a self-referential metric satisfies INV-110 while hiding the loss. (Complements INV-110 and INV-163.) (Constrains **INV-162**, which requires an embedded-of-referenced count: that count is a loss signal and MUST NOT be cited as a completeness measure — cross-referenced 2026-07-31.) (Source: `embedded-image-count-needs-an-external-denominator`, 2026-07-31.)
invariants.summary: A count or percentage presented as evidence of **completeness** MUST derive its denominator from outside the artifact it measures.

invariants.statement: An empty or absent field in one MCP tool's response is **NOT** evidence the server lacks the fact. Before recording that Senzing does not document X, the guide MUST also ask the tool that owns X in prose (`search_docs`), and MUST scope every negative finding to the tool and parameters actually asked — never to "the server". Observed: `get_sdk_reference(topic='flags', filter='SZ_WHY_ENTITIES_DEFAULT_FLAGS')` returns a one-line description with no `composite_members`, no `response_paths`, `applies_to` as the literal glob `["why_entities*"]`, and a `source_file` of the V3→V4 breaking-changes document — so the plugin's own "read the composite's `composite_members`" procedure appeared unrunnable, and the spec written from that observation proposed OR-ing sub-flags in blindly as the remedy. The membership was documented the whole time: `search_docs` returns, from the flags documentation, "The default recommended flags for `why_entities`. **Equivalent to: `SZ_INCLUDE_FEATURE_SCORES`**" — a single flag carrying no entity-name flag, which *explains* the `ENTITY_NAME: null` symptom instead of working around it, and is independently corroborated by the binding defaults in the same response's `method_signatures`. The correct order is: structured tool, then prose tool, then explicit sub-flags as a last resort with what could not be confirmed recorded (INV-080/INV-149). Distinct from INV-149, which is scoped to `response_schemas` and governs *retry* behavior ("empty is coverage, not a failed call") and did not prevent this: the failure is not retrying, it is concluding **absence** from one tool's silence. Distinct from INV-169, which forbids over-generalizing a positive observation into an absolute about a method; this forbids the negative form. (Complements INV-115, INV-149 and INV-169.) (Source: `why-entities-default-flags-has-no-composite-members`, 2026-07-31.)
invariants.summary: An empty or absent field in one MCP tool's response is **NOT** evidence the server lacks the fact.

invariants.statement: Every container the bootcamp starts MUST be recorded with the `runtime` that started it (`docker`, `podman`, or Apple's `container`), and every lifecycle action — the SessionEnd stop, the SessionStart state probe, and the resume message — MUST dispatch on that recorded runtime rather than assuming Docker. An entry with no `runtime` MUST be treated as `docker`, so progress files from earlier runs keep working. A runtime outside the recorded set MUST be reported but never executed, so a value in a progress file cannot become a binary a hook invokes. No session-boundary message may name a tool that did not start the container: naming the wrong CLI is what makes the message untrustworthy rather than merely unhelpful. (Generalizes INV-101, whose Docker-only wording assumed the single runtime available when it was written; the warn-and-continue contract is unchanged.) (Source: `container-lifecycle-hooks-assume-docker`, 2026-08-11.)

The onboarding preface's overview MUST name the bootcamp-feedback trigger phrase in bootcamper-facing text before the first content module, as a statement and never a 👉 question, and MUST say that using it does not cost the bootcamper their place (INV-074's exit banner returns them to the pending question). It is explanatory output — suppressed under the `minimal` verbosity preset and one line under `concise` **where a preset is readable** (INV-011/INV-012, the treatment INV-096 gives the time estimate; on a fresh run none exists yet, INV-075/INV-133, so it is simply shown) — and MUST NOT be repeated at every module start. Graduation's closing invitation is retained in addition, never instead. INV-010 guarantees the capability at any time, but a control announced only in the guide's own rules, in one mid-bootcamp module and at graduation is reachable only by bootcampers who already knew the phrase, which silently skews every feedback entry the project receives toward people told out of band. (Source: `feedback-trigger-is-never-taught-to-the-bootcamper`, 2026-08-11.)

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
