Observed 2026-08-14: a three-source generated Customer 360 scenario scored 100.0/100.0/100.0 with zero empty applicable fields — genuine scores, sanity-checked against sample values — so every source reached the ≥80% branch and **two of the three gate branches were unreachable on a first-class path**, taking with them the per-field completeness breakdown, the format-consistency diagnosis, the `issues` list and the per-`RECORD_TYPE` applicability reasoning (INV-174). A generated dataset that cannot fail the gate teaches the gate as a formality. Enforced by `tests/test_synthesized_scenario_has_quality_gaps.py`. (Source: `synthesized-scenarios-make-the-quality-gate-unreachable`, 2026-08-14.)

A prohibition that follows from a **general rule** MUST state that general rule and the property which triggers it, never only the forbidden token — so a reader can tell where it applies and, just as importantly, where it does **not**. Stated as a bare ban the rule generalizes wrongly and a guide that has correctly internalized it will refuse the one case where the forbidden thing is the documented remedy: concretely, "never pass `inline`" is right for `find_examples` and `generate_scaffold`, whose schemas do not declare it, and wrong for `download_resource`, whose schema does — the governing rule being INV-136 (only declared parameters may be passed), not anything about the word. ⚠️ **A prohibition MUST NOT be written so that obeying it faithfully strands the reader**, which is the failure this exists to prevent rather than mere tidiness. (Generalizes the clause recorded at INV-234, which remains the concrete MCP-listing case; this is the general statement and the one to cite for a prohibition outside that tool family. Sibling to INV-183 — that governs *where* a rule must be reachable, this governs *what* the rule must say to be followable.) Enforced by `tests/test_download_resource_is_a_listing.py`. (Source: `download-resource-returns-a-url-not-the-specification`, 2026-08-14; split out on maintainer review the same day.)
invariants.summary: A prohibition that follows from a **general rule** MUST state that general rule and the property which triggers it, never only the forbidden token — so a reader can tell where it applies and, just as importantly, where it does **not**.

invariants.statement: A guard for a rule about an artifact's **content** MUST assert that content, never a proxy for it — a dimension, a byte count, an exit status, or the presence of a file. The two come apart exactly where it matters most: measuring a page's `scrollHeight` and screenshotting at that height yields a PNG whose **height equals the page height while the bottom of the page is missing**, because `--headless=new` counts window chrome inside `--window-size`, so a height-only assertion passes the broken build (verified 2026-08-14: a 2671px page whose footer occupied 2613-2671 produced a 2671px PNG with white where the footer belonged; decoding the bottom rows found zero footer pixels). Where a proxy is unavoidable, the guard MUST say which proxy it is asserting and what it therefore cannot see. (Generalizes the ⛔ recorded at INV-235, which remains the concrete case for capture labels; this is the general statement and the one to cite for any other artifact. Sibling to INV-129, which requires the *run* to verify the rendered page rather than the exit status — this requires the same of the **test**.) Enforced by `tests/test_capture_single_page.py`. (Source: `single-page-capture-crops-to-the-viewport-and-calls-it-full-page`, 2026-08-14; split out on maintainer review the same day.)
invariants.summary: A guard for a rule about an artifact's **content** MUST assert that content, never a proxy for it — a dimension, a byte count, an exit status, or the presence of a file.

invariants.statement: Where shipped prose instructs the guide to author content that a **bundled script must parse**, that instruction MUST state the shape the script accepts. Prose that says *where* content goes without saying what *form* it must take is a contract with one half missing, and the half that loses is always the prose: the script simply does not match, and a guide that followed the instruction correctly produces a broken artifact at exit 0. Observed 2026-08-14: `module-completion.md` said to add visualization screenshots "to this module's **Actions Taken**" — which is a bulleted list — while `generate_recap_pdf.py` anchored its image detector to the start of the line, so a recap of **8** captured screenshots embedded **0**, reported success, and produced a `--check` line reading "captured 8, referenced 0" that names the guide as the culprit for the one thing it did not do. Stripping the `- ` markers and changing nothing else embedded 8 of 8. ⛔ **The safety net inherits the blind spot**, which is what makes this worse than a rendering bug: graduation's orphaned-screenshot backfill embeds captures "the recap does not already reference", and by the broken detector's reckoning the recap referenced none — so the mechanism that exists to catch a missed embed had the same defect as the thing it guarded (INV-146). ⚠️ Stating the shape does **not** discharge the script's duty to be forgiving about content already written the other way; a tolerance added for that reason MUST say it is a rescue rather than a second supported style, or the prose and the tolerance drift into two competing instructions. (Generalizes INV-161, which states the one path shape at the same instruction and is the same class of defect — a detail that renders as silent absence. Distinct from INV-176, which governs a shape the *renderer* requires within a block; this governs the shape the **parser** requires of the line.) Enforced by `tests/test_recap_pdf_bulleted_images.py` and `tests/test_authored_shapes_are_stated.py`. (Source: `recap-screenshots-in-bullets-never-reach-the-pdf`, 2026-08-14.) ⚠️ **Coverage note, 2026-08-14 — the guard was widened on maintainer review, and found a second breach.** This invariant binds all shipped prose while its first guard checked one site, so `test_authored_shapes_are_stated.py` now sweeps every **Markdown** surface a bundled generator parses and reads each generator's `_NEW_LINE_LABELS` **from the generator itself** — adding an allowlisted label without telling the guide how to write it fails that file. ⛔ **Scope is Markdown deliberately, and the reason is the mechanism, not convenience**: the same scripts parse `bootcamp_progress.json`, `bootcamp_preferences.yaml` and `data_sources.yaml`, where a shape mismatch is **loud** — the stdlib parser raises and the step fails visibly. This invariant exists for the silent case, which is a Markdown property: the document still renders and still reads correctly to a human, and only the treatment is lost. The breach found: `phase1-query-visualize.md` told the guide to include "at least one **near-miss**" and to "State the measurement", both accurate prose, while the discoveries generator keys on the literal labels `**Near-miss (the one that teaches more):**` and `**Measurement:**` for its own-line layout — and `**Near-miss:**` alone does **not** match, since `_normalize` maps it to `near miss` against an allowlist entry of `near miss the one that teaches more`. The recap side was already compliant, which is what made the asymmetry visible.
invariants.summary: Where shipped prose instructs the guide to author content that a **bundled script must parse**, that instruction MUST state the shape the script accepts.

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: A **per-source figure reported to the Bootcamper** MUST be reconciled against that source's own input count before it is shown; an unreconciled or mismatching figure MUST NOT be printed as a result. Reporting the aggregate is not reconciliation and does not discharge this: the defect that motivated it produces per-source numbers that sum to exactly the right total. ⛔ **A wrong number is more dangerous than a blank field**, which is why this is a MUST rather than a recommendation. INV-115's silent-blank class at least renders something a reader can notice; a plausible, monotonic, correctly-summing count invites no second look at all. Observed 2026-08-14 on a Phase C orchestrator built exactly as step 17 describes: three sources of 10 / 10 / 8 records reported 10, then 20, then 28, while the load itself was **entirely correct** — 28 records, zero errors, the datastore holding precisely what it should. Only the reporting was wrong. The cause is that the loading scaffold `sdk_guide(topic='load')` returns is a standalone `main()` whose counters are process-global — `LoadViaFutures.java` declares `private static int errorCount / successCount / retryCount` (server 1.32.9, 2026-08-14) — which is correct for a program that runs once and exits, and wrong the moment an orchestrator calls it per source in one process. The same arithmetic conceals a genuine failure: a source loading **0 of 8** still shows a rising success count inherited from its predecessors. ⚠️ **Composing an MCP scaffold into an execution shape it was not written for is the general hazard**; the scaffold is not defective and MUST NOT be "fixed" — the orchestrator either scopes the counters it owns or runs each source in its own process (INV-002: state the choice in binding-neutral terms, since module-level and global state are the equivalents outside Java). (Generalizes **INV-228**, which requires the same per-source count check and the same stop-on-mismatch for a dataset *written* from the MCP server; this extends the discipline from acquisition to any per-source figure the Bootcamper is shown.) Enforced by `tests/test_module06_orchestrator_guidance.py`. (Source: `orchestrator-per-source-stats-vs-static-scaffold-counters`, 2026-08-14.) ⚠️ **Forward pointer, 2026-08-14 — nothing here is superseded.** The trailing clause above — *an unreconciled or mismatching figure MUST NOT be printed as a result* — was extracted to **INV-245** on maintainer review, so that each invariant states one condition. What remains here is the **reconciliation requirement**, which still binds in full: reconcile the per-source figure against that source's own input before showing it, and note that the aggregate summing correctly does not discharge it. Cite **INV-245** for what must happen when a check disagrees, or for any verified value outside the per-source-count case; the clause is kept in this entry's text because `INVARIANTS.md` rule 1 forbids deleting an invariant's text and rule 2 permits editing only for meaning-preserving wording (the INV-234 → INV-240 precedent).
invariants.summary: A **per-source figure reported to the Bootcamper** MUST be reconciled against that source's own input count before it is shown; an unreconciled or mismatching figure MUST NOT be printed as a result.

invariants.statement: Where a bootcamp state field is written only **conditionally**, a step branching on it MUST NOT read that field's absence as a measured finding. Absence there means *not asked*, and a branch that converts it into an answer reports a measurement nobody took. The remedy is to measure the value at that step and persist it, or — where it cannot be measured — to say plainly that the value is being assumed and name what could not be determined; what is forbidden is presenting the assumption as the detected value. Observed 2026-08-14 in Module 6 Phases A **and** B, whose identical third branch read *"absent or null → no custom license was detected, so the default-limit note is the right assumption. Relay it."* The only writer of `license_record_limit` is Module 4's Step 8a gate, which is **volume-gated by design** and never fires for a small dataset — so the field is absent no matter what license is installed. On the walk that found it, `SzProduct.getLicense()` reported `recordLimit: 0` (no cap) while the field was absent, so the guide would relay a 500-record limit, and `sdk_guide`'s sampling prescription with it, to a Bootcamper with no cap at all — shrinking the dataset and under-demonstrating the very cross-source resolution Modules 6 and 7 exist to show. ⚠️ **The tell is a field whose writer is gated on something other than the question being asked**: `license_record_limit` reads like "the detected limit" and is really "the limit Module 4 happened to record while asking a volume question". Where such a value is one call away on this machine, the measured value governs the generic note (INV-012) and the step MUST take that call rather than infer from silence. (Sibling to **INV-194**, which forbids the same inference on the other surface — concluding the *server* lacks a fact from one tool's empty response; this forbids concluding the *Bootcamper's environment* lacks one from the bootcamp's own unwritten state. Complements INV-220, which governs which recorded provenance a branch reads, not what an unrecorded value means.) Enforced by `tests/test_module06_license_reconciliation.py` (the two Module 6 branches) and, plugin-wide, by `tests/test_no_absence_branch_asserts_a_licensing_finding.py`. (Source: `license-limit-assumed-when-it-could-be-measured`, 2026-08-14.) ⚠️ **Scope note, 2026-08-14 — nothing above is superseded; this states which cases the condition reaches.** Absence **is** sound evidence where the field's writer is gated on the **same question** the branch is asking, and such a branch is legal. `test_load_status` is the worked example on the permitted side: it too is written only conditionally (`module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase3-test-load.md` writes `skipped`; `module-06-data-processing/phaseB-load-first-source.md` writes `complete`), and Phase A's pre-load check reads its absence as *"a brief test load is owed"* — which is correct, because the writer of that field **is** the test load, so nothing having written it means no test load ran. `license_record_limit` differs precisely here: its writer is a **volume gate**, not a license check, so its silence carries no information about the license. ⚠️ **Dated correction, 2026-08-31 — the RULE is unchanged; two sentences of its 2026-08-14 evidence are now historical.** This invariant's own rationale says *"The only writer of `license_record_limit` is Module 4's Step 8a gate"* and *"the field is absent no matter what license is installed"*. Both described the plugin as it stood, and both stopped being true when **SDK setup's Step 5a** began measuring the installed license and persisting the result (`sdk-setup-step5a-reads-absence-as-the-built-in-license`, implemented on the maintainer's persist decision). That change was made *because* of this invariant — Step 5a was the second site of the defect, found by a live walk, and the remedy clause above prescribes it verbatim: *where such a value is one call away on this machine, the step MUST take that call rather than infer from silence.* What the condition forbids is unchanged, and absence still means **not measured**: it now means the measurement was skipped or failed rather than never attempted. ⛔ **A guard scoped to one module is what let the second site ship**, which is why the plugin-wide enforcer above was added alongside the module-scoped one rather than replacing it. ⛔ **The test is what the writer is gated on, not whether the write is conditional** — nearly every state field in the bootcamp is written conditionally, so conditionality alone would forbid correct branches throughout. Recorded because both branches were authored in the same session and the invariant, read literally and without this note, would send a later audit to "fix" the Phase A branch back into the defect `de73e72` had just removed. (⚠️ **The writer count in this entry is SUPERSEDED, corrected 2026-09-03 — no meaning change to the rule.** SUPERSEDED-COUNT: the sentence above reading *"The only writer of `license_record_limit` is Module 4's Step 8a gate"* was true when observed on 2026-08-14 and is not true now. The set was **five write sites across four steps** by 2026-08-28, and **six** once SDK setup's Step 5a became a writer on 2026-08-31. ⛔ **The rule never rested on the count, and no corrected count belongs here either** — what makes absence uninformative about the license is that **no step writes the field without measuring it**, a property that held before both corrections and will hold when a seventh writer appears. `counting-the-writers-of-license-record-limit-is-the-wrong-invariant` (2026-08-28) removed every count from shipped prose and left a guard that rejects a count **at any value, including the true one**; this entry was not brought forward with it, so the first of the three wrong counts stood here for six days in the invariant those sites cite as their authority. ⚠️ **The volume-gating clause still stands** — Step 8a fires only when collected volume approaches the limit — and so does everything the rule requires; only the arithmetic of who writes the field is corrected. ⛔ **This is also the vocabulary correction:** for a field written only from a measurement, the accurate gloss of absence is *never measured*, not *not asked*, which is the general wording above. Nothing asks the Bootcamper for this value, and INV-170 gives *asked* a different meaning — a value the Bootcamper was asked for outranks a detected one — so *not asked* points at asking them when the remedy is one SDK call. The general clause is correct for conditionally-written fields generally and is unchanged. Source: `inv-244-still-carries-the-writer-count-its-own-guard-rejects`, 2026-09-03.)
invariants.summary: Where a bootcamp state field is written only **conditionally**, a step branching on it MUST NOT read that field's absence as a measured finding.

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: A value that failed its own verification check MUST NOT be presented to the Bootcamper as a result; the discrepancy is reported in its place. This governs what happens **after** a check disagrees, which is a different subject from whether the check is performed — a step can reconcile diligently and still print the number it just disproved, and that is the worst of both, because the artifact now carries a figure the run itself knows to be wrong while looking like it was verified. ⛔ **Reporting the discrepancy is not optional and is not a log line**: the Bootcamper sees the failure, in the same place the value would have appeared, so an absent result is never mistaken for a real one. Where the value is load-bearing for a later step, the step stops rather than passing the disproved figure downstream. (Extracted from **INV-243** on maintainer review, 2026-08-14, so that each states one condition — INV-243 requires the reconciliation, this requires the honest disposal of its failure. The same split shape as INV-234 → INV-240. Generalizes beyond per-source counts to any verified value, and is the positive-value counterpart of the ground rules' *"Never present a blank value as a real result: say 'no value returned for X' so the failure is visible"* under INV-115 — that governs a value that never arrived, this governs one that arrived and failed its check.) Enforced by `tests/test_module06_orchestrator_guidance.py`. (Source: `orchestrator-per-source-stats-vs-static-scaffold-counters`, 2026-08-14; split out on maintainer review the same day.)
invariants.summary: A value that failed its own verification check MUST NOT be presented to the Bootcamper as a result; the discrepancy is reported in its place.

invariants.statement: A guard that enforces a rule across **multiple shipped sites** MUST derive its site set by scanning the corpus, never by hardcoding a list of paths. A hardcoded list encodes the author's belief about where the rule applies, and that belief is exactly what is wrong when a rule is applied incompletely — so the guard certifies the sites the implementer already thought of and is structurally blind to the one they missed. A derived guard fails on a site nobody thought of, including sites added later, which is the only way a *class* of defect stays fixed rather than an instance. ⛔ **A spec's own enumeration of its sites is a claim like any other and is not evidence.** Observed 2026-08-14: `license-limit-assumed-when-it-could-be-measured` closed with a section titled *"The same branch exists twice"*, naming two files; the branch existed **three** times, and the third — `module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md`, upstream of both and governing the paragraph where the sampling decision is actually made — shipped unfixed, guarded by a test that named the same two paths. The same session produced a second instance: INV-243 was cited only at the site where its defect was discovered, in a file whose own gate skips it unless the Bootcamper has two or more sources, while the paths every Bootcamper takes went uncovered. ⚠️ **`coverage_reports.py shipped` cannot substitute for this**: it reports invariants cited by *no* shipped file, so a rule cited once scores as covered. It answers "is this mentioned anywhere?", never "is it mentioned everywhere it binds?" — which is why the derivation belongs in the guard rather than in a report. Where a site legitimately words the rule differently, the assertion is scoped with its reason rather than the sweep being abandoned (a wording check swept across sites that legitimately differ starts failing on correct content). Enforced by `tests/test_module06_license_reconciliation.py`. (Source: `inv244-absent-license-branch-exists-in-module-4-too`, 2026-08-14.)
invariants.summary: A guard that enforces a rule across **multiple shipped sites** MUST derive its site set by scanning the corpus, never by hardcoding a list of paths.

invariants.statement: Every 👉 question presented to the Bootcamper MUST trace to a step in a shipped skill file; the guide MUST NOT originate a gate the bootcamp does not specify, and MUST NOT present a session- or host-level control — auto mode, auto-accept edits, permission mode, plan mode, fast mode, background tasks, `/compact`, `/loop` — as a bootcamp question, whether or not the host surfaces that control alongside the bootcamp. The model/effort switch (INV-063/INV-098/INV-158/INV-236) is the **only** Claude-interface control the bootcamp asks the Bootcamper to operate. ⛔ **The 👉 protocol governed a question's count, shape and placement, and nothing governed where it came from.** INV-005 fixes the count, INV-008/INV-009/INV-051 the shape, INV-211 and INV-224 the placement, INV-056 the verbatim wording of pinned gates — so a question tracing to no step in any skill file breached nothing on the books. INV-012 does not reach it either: it suppresses output the Bootcamper cannot act on, and a session toggle is something they *can* act on; it simply is not the bootcamp's to offer. Observed twice on 2026-08-15 on plugin 0.5.0: the Claude Code host prompt "Set up auto mode for your environment?" — the harness's own dialog, offering "Set it up" / "Not now" / "Don't show again" — appeared during the onboarding preface with `👉 Do you have any questions before we get started?` pending and unanswered, and the Bootcamper responded by filing feedback. A repo-wide search for that question and every related control returned zero matches — no plugin file asks it. ⚠️ **The sole exception is what made the unsanctioned question plausible, so the limit is stated where the precedent is set**, not only in the protocol 600 lines earlier: the bootcamp already asks the Bootcamper to operate `/model` and `/effort`, and a Bootcamper who has been asked that has no way to tell an "auto-mode?" question from bootcamp content. Answering a Bootcamper's *own* question about a host control is not a new gate — the one-sentence answer precedes the re-presented pending 👉 (INV-005), which is the any-time-controls path, not a new one. ⚠️ **A file-reading guard cannot detect a runtime-improvised question** — this defect exists in no file — so `tests/test_no_host_control_is_offered_as_a_question.py` asserts only that the rule ships and that no shipped 👉 line names a host control beyond `/model` and `/effort`; a clean run is not evidence the defect cannot recur. (Source: `a-question-with-no-origin-in-a-skill-file-reached-the-bootcamper`, 2026-08-15.) (⚠️ **Observation corrected 2026-08-15, no meaning change.** The MUST condition above is unchanged and was not edited. The original observation read "a Bootcamper **was asked** about auto-mode", which frames a harness dialog as a question the guide put to them. A second report the same day — a fresh run, three hours later — quoted the prompt with its three native options, UI chrome a model cannot emit, establishing it as **host-rendered** with the guide originating nothing. ⛔ **No run has yet shown a guide improvising a host-control question**, so this invariant is prophylaxis against a hazard the reports *do* demonstrate — a Bootcamper cannot tell an interface question from bootcamp content — and not the repair of an observed guide defect; no site may imply otherwise. The same correction was applied to the two other sites that carried the original wording, `ground-rules.md` and `tests/test_no_host_control_is_offered_as_a_question.py`. Two further requirements ship under this ID rather than a new one, because both are the same closed-set condition reaching a case the original sites missed: the any-time-controls entry fires when a Bootcamper **raises** a host control in any form — including reporting that a host prompt merely appeared — and the answer MUST NOT name a dismissal affordance such as "Don't show again", since directing the Bootcamper to silence a host prompt directs them to operate a second Claude-interface control. Source: `host-rendered-control-prompt-interrupts-a-pending-question`, 2026-08-15.)

The feedback triage taxonomy is the closed set `plugin`, `mcp-server`, `both`, `host`, `unclear`, and **every** shipped site stating that set MUST state all five. ⛔ **`host` names a defect the bootcamper's Claude interface owns — a harness prompt, dialog, toggle or session control that neither the bootcamp nor Senzing ships.** It exists because the two-question discriminating test gives the wrong answer without it: a harness defect survives a perfect plugin **and** a perfect server, which the test mapped to `both` — *"the plugin repeated or failed to guard an **upstream** defect"* — when no upstream Senzing defect exists. `unclear` is equally wrong for it, meaning *the component cannot be identified*, when for this class it can be, exactly. Observed twice on 2026-08-15 on plugin 0.5.0, both times the Claude Code "Set up auto mode for your environment?" prompt appearing over a pending 👉 during the onboarding preface; **both entries recorded `unclear` and then wrote in the `Routing:` field itself that the option set could not express the case** — the plugin reporting its own enumeration as incomplete, in the field, in writing, twice in one day. ⚠️ **A `host` verdict does not mean there is nothing to fix here**: the bootcamp still owns what it *says* when the bootcamper raises the control (INV-247) and how it recovers a 👉 question the host displaced. Enforced by `tests/test_feedback_routing.py`, which derives the site set by scanning (INV-246) rather than listing it. (Source: `feedback-routing-has-no-verdict-for-a-defect-neither-component-owns`, 2026-08-15.)
invariants.summary: The feedback triage taxonomy is the closed set `plugin`, `mcp-server`, `both`, `host`, `unclear`, and **every** shipped site stating that set MUST state all five.

invariants.statement: Only the `mcp-server` and `both` verdicts MAY be offered for upstream submission; `plugin`, `host` and `unclear` MUST stay local, and the shipped rule MUST state *why* `host` cannot be forwarded. ⛔ **The reason is the destination, not the severity.** `submit_feedback` reaches **Senzing**, which does not ship the Claude Code harness — so a `host` report sent through it arrives at a party that cannot act on it, anonymously, with no reply channel for the bootcamper. There is no upstream path for that class from inside the bootcamp, and the local entry is the whole record. ⚠️ **Before `host` existed this held only by accident**: both 2026-08-15 reporters fell back to `unclear`, which happens to suppress the offer, while the taxonomy's own stated test yielded `both` — and `both` sends. Eligibility must follow from the verdict by rule rather than from which fallback a guide happens to choose. A rule stated without its reason is the shape a later editor relaxes (INV-240). Enforced by `tests/test_feedback_routing.py`. (Source: `feedback-routing-has-no-verdict-for-a-defect-neither-component-owns`, 2026-08-15.)
invariants.summary: Only the `mcp-server` and `both` verdicts MAY be offered for upstream submission; `plugin`, `host` and `unclear` MUST stay local, and the shipped rule MUST state *why* `host` cannot be forwarded.

invariants.statement: The Truth Set visualization step MUST NOT present an **empty** visualization as the workstation-verification step passing; where the visualization renders no entities, the step reports that as a **failure** and names the likely cause. ⛔ **This is the clause INV-077 dropped, restored as a testable condition rather than a purpose.** INV-038 said the Bootcamper "ALWAYS sees a dynamic web-app visualization of the Truth Set **to verify that Senzing works** on the Bootcamper's workstation"; INV-077 superseded it with a delivery-and-selection rule — *which* module produces the visualization and *when* — and an empty graph satisfies INV-077 completely. So between INV-077's supersession and this entry, nothing on the books made a blank render a failure, while `ground-rules.md` cited INV-077 as though it did. ⚠️ **The hazard is the silence, not the emptiness.** The observed path: an `internal://` connection string is adopted, every load reports success, and the visualization renders an empty graph three modules later with nothing naming the cause — so the requirement is that the **step** stop treating that as a pass, not that emptiness be impossible. The app already behaves correctly here (`senzing_viz_server.py` renders *"No entities to graph."* rather than a blank canvas); what was missing was any rule binding the step's interpretation of it. ⚠️ **Scope: this binds the step's REPORTING, and deliberately does not mandate a detection mechanism** — the maintainer chose this over a detect-and-confirm form on 2026-08-15, because the check itself is unverifiable offline (INV-108) and a criterion nobody can run is worse than a narrower rule that holds. Step 2.4's endpoint table is where it binds: `/api/stats` already returns `entities_total`, and `/api/merges` already requires "at least one multi-record entity". Enforced by `tests/test_truthset_visualization_reports_empty_as_failure.py`. (Source: `inv077-supersession-dropped-the-visualization-verification-guarantee`, 2026-08-15.)
invariants.summary: The Truth Set visualization step MUST NOT present an **empty** visualization as the workstation-verification step passing; where the visualization renders no entities, the step reports that as a **failure** and names the likely cause.

invariants.statement: A turn presented to the Bootcamper MUST NOT contain **two or more** 👉 questions: the guide asks exactly one per yielding turn and ends the turn on it. Questions the Bootcamper raises, and any-time controls they invoke, are not the guide's questions and do not count against this. ⛔ **This rule was stated in 13 shipped places, enforced with zero-tolerance framing, checked at runtime by `auto-test`'s transcript linter — and registered nowhere, for the plugin's whole history until 2026-08-15.** Six sites cited an authority for it and every one was wrong: **INV-005** is a *marker* rule in full (*"Each question to the Bootcamper is preceded by 👉"*), so a turn ending on three 👉-prefixed questions satisfies it completely; **INV-008** governs ambiguity and **INV-009** complexity. All 249 invariant entries were parsed and searched: four mentioned a per-turn count and all four were **scoped** — INV-063 (the model/effort switch), INV-064 (the accepted-switch continuation), INV-135 (the license-request flow) and INV-225 (an observation supporting the non-yielding-step rule). Those three scoped rules are **instances of this one, not exceptions to it**. ⚠️ **The zero case is INV-225**, whose *"a step with no 👉 … MUST NOT end a turn"* already forbids a yielding turn ending on none — so the two invariants together fix the count at **exactly one**, and this entry deliberately does not restate that clause (maintainer decision, 2026-08-15: duplicating a clause across two IDs is how they drift apart). ⚠️ **`ground-rules.md` calls a breach "the #1 bootcamper complaint"**, which is why the absence mattered: the rule most likely to be reconciled away by a careful editor was the one with no ID behind it, and two of this session's own conversational changes argue from "INV-005 forbids two 👉". ⛔ **Reading cannot establish compliance.** The only mechanism that checks the *behavior* is `auto-test`'s `transcript_lint.py`, against real transcripts; the offline suite (INV-108) can assert that this rule ships and is cited correctly and nothing more. `dry-run` phase 3 is where a live turn is judged. Enforced by `tests/test_one_question_per_turn_is_registered.py`. (Source: `the-one-question-per-turn-rule-is-registered-nowhere`, 2026-08-15.)
invariants.summary: A turn presented to the Bootcamper MUST NOT contain **two or more** 👉 questions: the guide asks exactly one per yielding turn and ends the turn on it.

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: Every read of a **bundled plugin file** — the `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest above all — MUST resolve inside the plugin serving the run: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…` when that variable is set and non-empty, otherwise the documented skill-relative fallback (`<this-skill-dir>/../../…`), otherwise "Unknown". ⛔ The guide MUST NOT search the filesystem for a bundled file and MUST NOT read one outside the resolved plugin root: two plugin roots on one machine is a normal state — an installed plugin plus a clone, or an upgrade whose old copy was never removed — so the first match a traversal reaches is not the plugin serving the run. An unresolvable value is reported as "Unknown", never guessed, and the resolved path is never written into a bootcamper-facing artifact (INV-065). Extends **INV-185** from *running* a bundled script to *reading* a bundled file: INV-185's fallback already shipped at five script-invocation sites, but both its scope and its guard stop at the interpreter, so the manifest reads had no fallback specified and an unset `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` left the guide to improvise. ⚠️ **A file-reading guard cannot watch this defect happen** — the search existed in no file — so `tests/test_plugin_manifest_reads_resolve_inside_the_plugin.py` asserts only that the rule ships, that every shipped manifest path resolves, and that the feedback hook injects a resolved version rather than a variable; a clean run is evidence the plugin no longer invites the search, not that it cannot recur. (Observed 2026-08-15 on plugin 0.5.1: the WELCOME banner showed `v0.5.0`, read from a second checkout on the same machine.) (Source: `plugin-version-resolves-to-the-running-plugin-root`, 2026-08-15.)

Every English word written in this repository MUST use its US spelling — shipped plugin prose, specs, invariants, tests, code comments and identifiers alike. Where US and British forms differ (`-ize`/`-yze` not `-ise`/`-yse`, `-or` not `-our`, `-er` not `-re`, `license` not `licence`, single `l` before a suffix), the US form is the only one that may be written. A file exempted from this rule MUST carry its reason. ⛔ **The convention existed nowhere for the plugin's whole history until 2026-08-16**, which is why the count reached four figures rather than a handful: an author reaching for a house style found none in `docs/development.md`, `ground-rules.md` or this file, so both spellings were equally defensible across ~370 specs and 42 shipped files. The sweep found **1,231 British word occurrences across 295 files**, plus **5 CamelCase class names the same sweep could not see on its first pass**. ⛔ **The repository was not what caught it.** The correction arrived from outside: someone read the published plugin in the public access repo, hand-corrected it there, and the edits returned through `/retrofit-from-public` as `2223961`. That retrofit then left the suite red and unnoticed until the next full run — `retrofit.sh` copies `plugins/`, `.claude-plugin/`, `docs/` and `README.md` but never `tests/`, so it moved shipped prose out from under the dev-only tests that pin it **verbatim**, breaking ten of them. ⚠️ **A clean guard run does not mean the corpus is US English.** INV-246 binds a multi-site guard to derive its *sites* by scanning, and this one does; it cannot derive its *vocabulary*, because the corpus is the thing being judged — so the word list is a genuine hardcoded list and under-detects by construction. It under-detects by one word **deliberately**: `analyses` is both the British verb and the correct US plural of `analysis`, so flagging it would fail on correct US prose. Stem matching is rejected outright (`organism`, `mechanism`, `parallelism`, `characteristic`, `equally`, `totally`, `radialLine` and `LabelLayoutAssertions` are all correct and all contain British-looking stems): matching is on whole words, after splitting identifiers on both `_` and CamelCase boundaries, which is what makes the CamelCase shape reachable at all. An exemption MUST be narrower than a whole file wherever it can be — a path plus the exact word **and count** it may carry — so that every other British form in that file still fails and a waiver whose word has gone fails as stale; and no marker may exist that a future edit can add to a line to silence it. Enforced by `tests/test_us_english_spelling.py`. (Source: `us-english-spelling-is-unregistered-and-unguarded`, 2026-08-16.)
invariants.summary: Every English word written in this repository MUST use its US spelling — shipped plugin prose, specs, invariants, tests, code comments and identifiers alike.

invariants.statement: At any time, a Bootcamper can capture a note — an idea, question, reminder, to-do or memo of their own — from onboarding, any module, or graduation. The **inward** counterpart to INV-010: feedback points outward (a `Routing:` verdict, the maintainer's triage input, possibly forwarded upstream), while a note is the Bootcamper's own thought about **their** work, carries no routing verdict and no who-noticed-it field (INV-116), has no upstream path at all, and is folded into their recap at graduation. ⛔ **When a message satisfies both vocabularies — "make a note that the bootcamp is broken" — it is FEEDBACK**, because naming the bootcamp, plugin, module or tutorial as the thing at fault makes it an attributed defect report that happens to be phrased as a note; routing it to notes would bury a defect report in a private keepsake the maintainer never sees, and nothing is lost by preferring feedback, which is also durable, also banner-bracketed and also resumes the pending question. That precedence MUST be stated in code rather than left to branch order. ⚠️ **The trigger MUST be anchored on an imperative to record something, never on the bare verb** — "make a note", "remind me", "jot this down", "don't let me forget", "remember to `<verb>`" fire; "do you remember", "note that `<claim>`", "as noted above" MUST NOT. In Modules 5-7 the Bootcamper is debugging their own code and asking the guide to recall things constantly, so a spurious capture there prepends a banner and a recital to a turn where they wanted a traceback explained; a missed capture is far cheaper, because the flow stays reachable by `/bootcamp-note` and by `notes.md` while a derailed debugging turn is not recoverable (INV-054's reasoning, applied to a second vocabulary). The control MUST be named in bootcamper-facing text during onboarding — an any-time control nobody is told about is an any-time control nobody uses. ⚠️ **Reviewed 2026-08-17: this entry deliberately bundles four rules** — the any-time control, the feedback precedence, the trigger vocabulary, and the onboarding disclosure. They were promoted here from the source spec's body during implementation, and the maintainer chose to keep them under one id rather than split them, since every clause traces to the same flow and splitting would cost a supersession. A citation of INV-254 should name which clause it means. Enforced by `tests/test_feedback_capture_triggers.py` and `tests/test_bootcamp_notes_flow.py`. (Source: `bootcamp-notes-capture-and-recap-section`, 2026-08-16.)
invariants.summary: At any time, a Bootcamper can capture a note — an idea, question, reminder, to-do or memo of their own — from onboarding, any module, or graduation.

invariants.statement: The note capture flow MUST be bracketed by pinned-verbatim banners: a 📌 "BOOTCAMP NOTE" entry banner before its first 👉 question, and a 📌 "NOTE SAVED — BACK TO THE BOOTCAMP" exit banner (a statement) after the note is confirmed saved and before the pending bootcamp 👉 question is re-presented. ⛔ **The glyph MUST differ from the feedback flow's 📝 (INV-074).** Two any-time flows opening with the same glyph are two flows the Bootcamper cannot tell apart at a glance, which is the entire reason INV-074 exists. Both banners are statements and never count against INV-251. Enforced by `tests/test_bootcamp_notes_flow.py`. (Source: `bootcamp-notes-capture-and-recap-section`, 2026-08-16.)
invariants.summary: The note capture flow MUST be bracketed by pinned-verbatim banners: a 📌 "BOOTCAMP NOTE" entry banner before its first 👉 question, and a 📌 "NOTE SAVED — BACK TO THE BOOTCAMP" exit banner (a statement) after the note is confirmed saved and before the pending bootcamp 👉 question is re-presented.

invariants.statement: Every approved note MUST be appended to `docs/bootcamp_notes.md` — never rewritten over — and confirmed present on disk by a re-read before the Bootcamper is told it was saved. This is INV-067's discipline applied to the notes file and for the same reason: a note the Bootcamper was told was saved and which is not on disk is worse than one they know was never captured. A failed write, a failed re-read or an unreachable notes file warns in one line and returns them to the bootcamp — a note is never a gate (INV-048). Enforced by `tests/test_bootcamp_notes_flow.py`. (Source: `bootcamp-notes-capture-and-recap-section`, 2026-08-16.)
invariants.summary: Every approved note MUST be appended to `docs/bootcamp_notes.md` — never rewritten over — and confirmed present on disk by a re-read before the Bootcamper is told it was saved.

invariants.statement: A note MUST be recited to the Bootcamper for approval before it is saved, MUST be stored in the Bootcamper's own words, and any bootcamp-authored elaboration or context MUST be stored under its own label — never merged into the Bootcamper's text — and MUST remain visibly attributed where it is rendered. ⛔ **This is a keepsake with their name on the certificate.** A paragraph they did not write, indistinguishable from one they did, is the plugin putting words in their mouth permanently, in the one artifact they keep. The note's **type** (`idea` | `question` | `reminder` | `to-do` | `memo`) is assigned silently as an assessment and MUST NOT be asked for: they reported a thought, naming its kind is the plugin's job, and a 👉 spent on a taxonomy is a 👉 spent on nothing they care about. The machine-composed context block is bound by INV-065 — no hostname, username, home-directory path or IP address. Enforced by `tests/test_bootcamp_notes_flow.py`. (Source: `bootcamp-notes-capture-and-recap-section`, 2026-08-16.)

When the recap carries a `<!-- BOOTCAMP-NOTES:START/END -->` section, the recap PDF MUST render it between the last module page and the Certificate of Completion in **both** renderers (INV-066), MUST list it in the table of contents where the renderer has one, MUST count its characters toward the content-retention figure (INV-110), and MUST NOT treat it as a module — it never appears in the certificate's module citation (INV-100), in either renderer's cover module list, or in the four-subsection completeness check (INV-103). ⛔ **The fence is the discriminator, never the heading text.** `parse_recap` turns every `## ` heading into a module section, so a notes section recognized by its *title* is one renamed module away from being mis-parsed — and a Bootcamper's private note one heading away from being printed on their certificate. The block is therefore lifted out of the source **before** module parsing begins; an **unterminated** fence runs to end of text rather than being treated as absent, because graduation appends the block after the last module, so losing the closing marker must cost the notes' formatting at worst and never promote a note to a module. ⚠️ **The retention clause is the one whose omission is silent and severe.** The figure is rendered-over-source characters, so notes counted in the source but not in the rendered total make retention fall with every note the Bootcamper writes — their own words scored as content the PDF lost — and a long enough notes file crosses `MIN_CONTENT_RETENTION` and makes the generator **refuse to render their recap at all**. The count is taken at parse time from the lines the parser actually placed, not recomposed from the fields, so label markup the renderer draws as a stamp is not scored as loss while a note that fails to parse still is. The fold at graduation is append-only and idempotent (INV-085), writes **nothing at all** when there are no notes — an empty notes section on a keepsake is worse than an absent one — and never touches a module section. ⚠️ **Reviewed 2026-08-17:** the unterminated-fence rule and the parse-time retention count are **implementation decisions**, not the source spec's text — the spec specified neither. Both were kept on maintainer review because each prevents a distinct silent failure: a truncated write promoting a private note onto the Certificate of Completion, and retention falling with every note the Bootcamper writes. Enforced by `tests/test_recap_notes_section.py` (PDF) and `tests/test_bootcamp_notes_flow.py` (the Markdown fold). (Source: `bootcamp-notes-capture-and-recap-section`, 2026-08-16.)

A graph node's visual encoding — **fill, stroke and stroke width alike** — MUST derive from the entity's whole **set** of data sources, joined and sorted, never from one member of it; the palette MUST be allocated in a **single pass** over every source and every observed combination together; and any combination color the graph draws MUST be **named in the legend**. A single-source entity degenerates to its own source code, which is what makes the rule backward-compatible. ⛔ **Coloring by the first source renders every cross-source entity as single-source under a legend that says so**, and it is invisible on a dataset whose entities mostly sit in one source — which is why it survived the Truth Set. (Observed 2026-08-17: 1,951 cross-source entities rendered in the single-source `GLEIF` color. Two separate palette-allocation calls each restart at the top of the palette and reproduce the collision, which is why the single pass is part of the rule.) Binds every implementation, not only the bundled Python reference (INV-090/INV-124). Enforced by `tests/test_graph_colors_by_source_combination.py`. (Source: `seven-hard-rules-shipped-in-one-run-with-no-invariant`, 2026-08-17.)

A visualization server MUST bind the **loopback** interface explicitly and MUST NOT bind the wildcard address, and MUST confirm — before its URL is handed to the Bootcamper — that the process answering `/api/stats` is the one just started, by comparing a **per-process nonce** rather than any figure two runs of the same project would agree on. A disagreement stops the step and reports the conflict; it MUST NOT degrade to a warning above a working link. ⛔ **A successful bind is not proof the port was free:** a wildcard bind coexists with an existing loopback listener, and either process may then answer. (Observed 2026-08-17 on macOS: a three-week-old server from an unrelated project held `127.0.0.1:8080`, this one bound `*:8080` successfully, and only luck decided which answered a localhost request; the other outcome shows a stranger's dataset under the Bootcamper's project title, captured into the recap screenshots.) Binds every implementation, not only the bundled Python reference (INV-002/INV-090/INV-124). Enforced by `tests/test_viz_server_bind_and_identity.py`. (Source: `seven-hard-rules-shipped-in-one-run-with-no-invariant`, 2026-08-17.)

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: A **cross-source join prediction** carries its evidence or its absence. Where shipped guidance has the guide name an expected cross-source pair in a Bootcamper-facing deliverable, the claim MUST be labeled either **measured** — backed by a count of distinct values shared on the **named** attribute — or explicitly **candidate, overlap unmeasured**. ⛔ **A grouped completeness score is not evidence for a per-attribute claim:** presence-of-any answers whether a record carries an identifier at all, while a join needs presence-of-**same**. (Observed 2026-08-17: two sources both scoring IDENTIFIER 100% were written up as the highest-confidence pair "both carrying LEI" when exactly one LEI value was shared in the whole dataset — wrong by ~38x, disproved only after loading. ⚠️ Deliberately scoped to cross-source join predictions rather than to predictions generally, so the rule stays next to the evidence that produced it — maintainer decision, 2026-08-17.) Enforced by `tests/test_group_score_is_not_a_join_prediction.py`. (Source: `seven-hard-rules-shipped-in-one-run-with-no-invariant`, 2026-08-17.)
invariants.summary: A **cross-source join prediction** carries its evidence or its absence.

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: Where the SDK runs in a **Linux environment while the project resides on a mounted host filesystem**, the datastore's placement MUST be **measured before it is created**, using the diagnostic the server prescribes, and the measurement MUST be reported to the Bootcamper; and any relocation offered MUST remain within the project directory (INV-200). The datastore is reached over a translation layer rather than a native one in that configuration — the signature cases are **WSL2 with the project under `/mnt/`** and a Docker bind mount — and nothing fails: it is one to two orders of magnitude slower, so an assumption is indistinguishable from a measurement until the load is already slow. ⛔ The call and its argument MUST be taken from the server at the point of use rather than from shipped prose (INV-080); `SzDiagnostic.check_repository_performance` is the instrument as of MCP server 1.33.0, 2026-08-21, and naming it here is illustration, not authority. (Wording narrowed at sign-off, 2026-08-21: an earlier draft said the default location "MUST NOT change without their explicit consent", which read as though consent could authorize what INV-200 forbids. Placement is INV-200's; this invariant owns the measuring and the reporting.) Enforced by `tests/test_datastore_mount_crossing_is_measured.py`. (Source: `the-2026-08-21-run-shipped-three-unregistered-guarantees`, 2026-08-21.)

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: Generated data-source registration MUST be safe to re-run **by construction** — load, register, export, register the config, replace the default id — and MUST NOT depend on an error being raised for an already-registered code, which `get_sdk_reference(topic='parameters', filter='register_data_source')` documents for no binding (server **1.33.0, 2026-08-21**): it returns `register_data_source(data_source_code: str) -> str` with warnings only about argument types across bindings and no error condition. A per-code catch is a permitted **fallback** and MUST NOT be the mechanism — code whose idempotency rests on it is untested by construction and fails in exactly the case it was written for. The re-runnability comes one call **later** than the per-code registration: registering an identical configuration returns the existing config ID rather than failing. ⛔ No binding's exception type may be named as a contract (INV-002). (**Narrows INV-089**, which requires the codes to be registered "idempotently" — the *property* — and is silent on the *mechanism*, which is the gap this closes. INV-089 is **not** superseded; both bind, and an implementation satisfying INV-089 alone may still rest on a caught error. Two statement sites — `module-06-data-processing/phaseA-build-loading.md` and `module-03-system-verification/phase1-verification.md` — with five files referring to them.) Enforced by `tests/test_registration_idempotency_is_constructed.py`. (Source: `the-2026-08-21-run-shipped-three-unregistered-guarantees`, 2026-08-21.)

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: A quality band MUST NOT by itself route the Bootcamper into remediation. Where a band's cause may be a **data characteristic** rather than a mapping defect, the step MUST establish which before offering a remediation loop, MUST state plainly when remediation would not help, and MUST record the finding either way. The possible-match rate is driven mostly by things a remap cannot change — how populated each field is in the source, how common the names are, and how large the dataset is (`reporting_guide(topic='evaluation', language='<chosen_language>')`, server **1.33.0, 2026-08-21**) — and on the generated-scenario path the plugin **creates** those characteristics itself, since INV-239 requires a source gapped into the 70-79% band. So a band that looks remediable is routinely not. **Three sites, each honoring this by a different mechanism, which is why the rule is stated as a property rather than a procedure:** `module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md` (the possible-match rate has three outcomes and only the mapping-actionable one reaches Module 5), `module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase1-quality-assessment.md` (a sub-70% completeness score on a source with high NAME/ADDRESS coverage is a probable **applicability** error, so the record-type mix is checked before the score is reported or anyone is routed), and `module-06-data-processing/phaseD-validation.md` (a high-share cross-source suppressor is reported as a **FINDING**, never a pass/fail). ⛔ A future band-routing step is bound by this even though all three current sites already satisfy it; that is the point of registering it (INV-246 — a rule's site list is not its site set). Enforced by `tests/test_poor_band_requires_a_mapping_cause.py`. (Source: `the-2026-08-21-run-shipped-three-unregistered-guarantees`, 2026-08-21.)
invariants.summary: A quality band MUST NOT by itself route the Bootcamper into remediation.

invariants.statement: Any check the plugin or its guards perform by **matching, counting or comparing** MUST establish that its input is non-empty before reporting a result, and MUST report an empty match as a **failed or unrun check** — never as agreement, and never as a pass. Where a check compares two sides, **both** sides MUST be asserted non-empty. A test whose assertion can be satisfied by an empty input MUST carry an explicit anti-vacuity assertion naming the floor it requires. ⛔ **The failure mode is silence, which is why this cannot be left to attention:** an emptied input produces a passing check indistinguishable from a correct one, and every instance on record was found by accident rather than by a check — a tab-set comparison that matched `data-tab="…"`, found zero in both files and reported *"tab sets match: True"* when `data-tab` appears nowhere in the generated app; two hook assertions keyed off `resolved_args()` that passed while asserting nothing once the scripts moved, the tell being a 0.000s run that spawned no subprocess; `conformance.py rules` reading clean while its pattern missed 145 mid-line rules; and a malformed ledger heading being *absent* rather than invalid to `(?m)^## (\S+)$`, so every entry-level guard skipped it silently. (Generalizes the shape **INV-129** and **INV-218** state for their own subjects — verify the rendered artifact rather than the exit status, verify the installed artifact rather than the installer's exit code — both of which remain binding as written; **INV-188** is the same concern for a string a script emits. What none of them covers is a comparison whose operands were empty.) (Source: `a-check-that-matches-nothing-must-not-report-agreement`, 2026-08-23.)
invariants.summary: Any check the plugin or its guards perform by **matching, counting or comparing** MUST establish that its input is non-empty before reporting a result, and MUST report an empty match as a **failed or unrun check** — never as agreement, and never as a pass.

invariants.statement: An exemption from a generator's **dropped-character report** MUST be scoped to an **identified passage**, never to a character, and MUST leave the character dropped from the rendered page (INV-143 — never substituted with `?`). Every exemption MUST name the exact passage it covers, MUST be evaluated against the full normalized passage **before** any excerpt truncation, and MUST NOT prevent the same character being reported when it appears anywhere else in the document — including when the exempt passage is rendered first. An exemption is admissible **only** where the dropped text is a machine-readable marker the plugin itself mandates, read from the source document and never from the rendered artifact, so that neither remedy branch of the warning applies. ⛔ **An exemption MUST NOT be added because a warning is frequent or inconvenient.** (INV-159 requires the loss be reported and says nothing about suppressing the report, which is the gap this closes: the report is the only thing between the Bootcamper and silent content loss on the artifact they frame — a Bootcamper once received `?? (Li Ming)` at 34 pt with exit 0 and no warning. A guaranteed warning with no correct response is what teaches that warnings are ignorable, which is why the first exemption exists and why the next one needs the same test. The rendered-first clause is not hypothetical: the collector is keyed by character and returns early on a repeat, so exempting at report time rather than record time would let the exempt passage consume the slot a genuine later occurrence needs.) Enforced by `tests/test_generated_scenario_marker_drop_is_exempt.py`. (Source: `a-renderer-warning-exemption-must-be-scoped-to-a-passage`, 2026-08-23.)
invariants.summary: An exemption from a generator's **dropped-character report** MUST be scoped to an **identified passage**, never to a character, and MUST leave the character dropped from the rendered page (INV-143 — never substituted with `?`).

invariants.statement: Where a step must choose **one item from an MCP tool's listing response**, the selection criterion MUST be a **property of the item** the step can test — what the code does, what a field contains — and MUST NOT be the item's position in the list, the list's length, or its filename. Every such step MUST name that property, and MUST name at least one listed item the property **excludes** wherever a plausible near-miss exists. A count or group list quoted at such a step is illustration only and MUST be marked as such. ⛔ **The rule exists because the counts move.** `generate_scaffold(workflow='full_pipeline')` returned 18 snippets across three groups on server 1.32.2 (2026-07-29) and 22 across four on 1.32.9 (2026-08-14) — a whole group appeared — while the two snippets Module 3 Step 4 names by shape stayed exactly where they were; `workflow='initialize'` returns 14 snippets on 1.33.0 (2026-08-23) with `content` absent and **no field marking any of them** as engine-creating. So a step written against a count breaks silently the next time the server indexes more, and a step written against a shape does not. ⚠️ **"Creates an engine" is the cautionary example of a criterion that is not a property.** Module 2 Step 9 must pick the initialization snippet that *exercises* an engine; both `initialization/engine_priming.py` and `initialization/abstract_factory.py` call `create_engine()`, so that phrase distinguishes nothing — the testable property is whether the body **invokes a method on** the engine, which is what that step's own ⛔ ("create **and use** an `SzEngine`") already demands. (Distinct from **INV-234**, which governs how a call site must *document* that a response is a listing, and from **INV-212**, which governs the query vocabulary that *reaches* the material: naming a route and selecting from its response are different acts, and INV-212 covers only the first — which is how this rule shipped twice, registered nowhere. **INV-160** governs the elision shape itself.) (Source: `selecting-from-an-mcp-listing-by-shape-is-unregistered`, 2026-08-23.)
invariants.summary: Where a step must choose **one item from an MCP tool's listing response**, the selection criterion MUST be a **property of the item** the step can test — what the code does, what a field contains — and MUST NOT be the item's position in the list, the list's length, or its filename.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: Before composing a flag set for an SDK call, the guide MUST confirm each composite flag's **representation** for the Bootcamper's chosen binding — not only its membership — via `get_sdk_reference(topic='parameters', filter='<method>', language='<binding>')`, which is the only route that reports a binding type. `topic='flags'` returns composites and single flags in **one shape**, with `composite_members` as the only difference and no field naming a type, byte-identical with and without the `language` argument (server **1.33.0**, 2026-08-26). Where the flags parameter is a **collection** and the binding declares the composite as a collection, the composite MUST be **merged into** the set rather than listed among its members. The rule MUST be stated as a **binding-shape property**, with any single language as illustration only (INV-002). ⛔ **The hazard is larger than a compile error: two classes one letter apart carry identical constant names with different types.** Verified against the installed `sz-sdk.jar` on 2026-08-26 (`javap`, then `javac`/`java`; observation-only per INV-080/INV-149 — no MCP route reports a binding's class layout): `com.senzing.sdk.SzFlag` is an enum that **also** declares `public static final Set<SzFlag>` fields for the composites, so `SzFlag.SZ_ENTITY_INCLUDE_ALL_RELATIONS` is a `Set` and **not** an enum constant; the identically-named `long` (value `960`) lives in the separate **plural** class `com.senzing.sdk.SzFlags`, which cannot be passed to a `Set<SzFlag>` parameter at all. So reaching for the plural class to escape the first error compiles and then fails at the call. ⚠️ **This sits directly on the path the reference itself recommends:** the same response that says to request exactly the flags whose output is consumed, rather than a `*_DEFAULT_FLAGS` composite, returns a list in which some entries cannot be used the way the others can and does not say which. (**Extends INV-132** from a method's parameter shapes to the **representation of the flag constants passed into them**; INV-132 reaches a composite's *availability* and stops short of its type.) (Source: `a-composite-flag-is-a-set-in-java-and-cannot-be-listed-among-enum-constants`, 2026-08-26.)

invariants.index_group: Platform, shell, encoding and file placement
invariants.statement: A step that verifies a **language binding** MUST report the **resolved path** the binding was loaded from, beside the engine version, and MUST NOT substitute a package-metadata or distribution version for it. The engine version answers through the **native library** and the binding through the runtime's **module search path**; only their agreement, evidenced by the path, verifies that the copy under test is the copy that shipped. The check MUST sit on a step **every** install path reaches, including one that skips installation because an SDK is already present. ⛔ **A shadowing distribution produces a working import and a plausible, current-looking version, so a step that merely reports success is what the defect hides behind.** Measured 2026-08-26 on a stock workstation: with `PYTHONPATH` unset, `import senzing` resolved to `~/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/senzing/__init__.py` while the SDK-shipped bindings sat unreachable at `/opt/senzing/er/sdk/python`, and every later module ran against a different SDK version than the one just verified. ⚠️ **Package metadata is NOT an acceptable substitute and must not be reached for:** the SDK-shipped Python binding exposes no `__version__`, and `importlib.metadata.version('senzing')` returned **4.1.2** — the PyPI distribution's number — for an import resolving to the SDK's own directory, because that directory ships no distribution metadata and the lookup falls through to `site-packages`. A version comparison built on it reports the shadowing package's version while the correct module is loaded: the same silent skew the check exists to catch, wearing the check's uniform. (Complements **INV-222**, which governs how the language packages are *installed and made available* — by path, sourced from `sdk_guide` at run time — and is silent on how a step proves *which copy loaded*.) Enforced by `tests/test_env_script_names_every_required_export.py`. (Source: `env-script-template-names-every-export-but-pythonpath`, 2026-08-26.)
invariants.summary: A step that verifies a **language binding** MUST report the **resolved path** the binding was loaded from, beside the engine version, and MUST NOT substitute a package-metadata or distribution version for it.

invariants.statement: A visualization the Bootcamper's code builds MUST expose, on its graph endpoint, the number of **distinct sorted source-set keys** over the nodes it emits, and the build step MUST compare that number against the count of distinct color keys the **legend names** before any screenshot is captured. Inequality means nodes are colored by one member of their source set (INV-259) and MUST **stop the step** — never capture first, because the screenshots persist into the recap and the production project. Fewer than two distinct keys means the check **could not fail** and MUST be reported as **not exercised**, never as a pass (INV-265). The requirement MUST be stated as behavior in the any-language contract: a check reaching generated code only through the bundled Python reference does not bind it (INV-002, and the failure INV-164 and INV-190 each had to record case by case). ⛔ **This exists because stating the rule three times did not work.** INV-259, the any-language contract and Module 7 step 3c all carried the source-set coloring rule, and on 2026-08-25 a Module 7 app generated in **Java** still colored from `data_sources[0]`: 294 of 5,619 cross-source entities rendered in a single-source color beneath a legend saying they were single-source. The bundled reference had been correct for eight days and the run was on a plugin containing that fix — so the defect reappeared where the rule had to be *followed* rather than *inherited*. ⚠️ **The check is required at both build sites because the rule must be *followed* rather than *inherited*** — the Java recurrence above happened on a plugin that already contained the correct reference. Enforced by `tests/test_encoding_self_check_is_stated_as_behavior.py`. (Source: `the-source-set-coloring-rule-is-stated-three-times-and-verified-nowhere`, 2026-08-26.) (Corrected 2026-08-28 by `the-truth-set-does-exercise-the-encoding-self-check`: as registered on 2026-08-26 this entry closed with *"The Truth Set structurally cannot provoke it (nearly all its entities sit in one source, where first-source coloring looks correct), which is why the check is required at both build sites and why the not-exercised outcome is the expected one there."* **That premise is false and is withdrawn.** The Truth Set registers **three** data sources — CUSTOMERS 120, REFERENCE 22, WATCHLIST 17, 159 records (`get_sample_data(dataset='truthset', source='list')`, server **1.33.0**, re-confirmed 2026-08-28) — and one full load on 2026-08-27 emitted **7** distinct source-set keys, **4** of them combinations, over 84 entities (observation, INV-080/INV-149). So the check **is** exercised at the Truth Set build site, a real `ok`/mismatch verdict is expected there, and a `not_exercised` result at either site is a signal that fewer sources loaded than expected. The rule itself is unchanged; only the false aside about which datasets can provoke the defect is withdrawn. The not-exercised requirement below two keys stands exactly as written (INV-265).)
invariants.summary: A visualization the Bootcamper's code builds MUST expose, on its graph endpoint, the number of **distinct sorted source-set keys** over the nodes it emits, and the build step MUST compare that number against the count of distinct color keys the **legend names** before any screenshot is captured.

invariants.statement: A completeness check whose denominator is a **set of produced artifacts** MUST also establish that the **expected** set of such artifacts was produced, from a source independent of them. For tab coverage the expected set is derived from `modules_completed` in `config/bootcamp_progress.json`, mapped to the visualization each producing module is specified to build; an expected artifact with **no manifest** MUST be reported by name, with the module that owed it, as an **unrun** check, and the overall coverage figure MUST be **withheld** rather than printed beside it (INV-163, INV-265). Reporting MUST NOT block production of the recap (INV-048). ⛔ **The failure is arithmetic invisibility, not a wrong number.** On 2026-08-25 the check reported *"6 of 6 captured tabs reached the recap"* — a clean pass — while the entire Module 7 application, built over the Bootcamper's own resolved data, had been captured not at all: it wrote no manifest, so it contributed no denominator and no shortfall anything could see. The recap PDF illustrated the whole bootcamp with six pictures of the demo Truth Set while the Bootcamper's cross-source entities and fraud leads appeared only as prose, which inverts which work was theirs in the artifact most likely to be shown to someone else. (**Extends INV-193** from the artifact being measured to the set of measurements themselves. INV-193 moved the denominator off the recap and onto the capture manifest — external to the recap, but still derived from whatever capture happened to produce, which is the same self-referential shape one layer out. A producer that emitted nothing contributes no denominator.) Enforced by `tests/test_expected_visualization_denominator.py`. (Source: `tab-coverage-has-no-denominator-for-a-visualization-that-wrote-no-manifest`, 2026-08-26.)
invariants.summary: A completeness check whose denominator is a **set of produced artifacts** MUST also establish that the **expected** set of such artifacts was produced, from a source independent of them.

invariants.statement: Where proceeding from a Bootcamper's answer requires **LOADING** anything — invoking a skill, reading a file, running a script — the acknowledgment of that answer MUST be emitted as bootcamper-visible text **BEFORE** the first such call, never composed into the reply that follows it. Tool calls produce no bootcamper-visible output, so an acknowledgment that trails the loading leaves the answer looking unregistered for the whole interval; at a module or graduation transition that interval spans several consecutive calls. The acknowledgment MUST be a **statement** — no 👉, no turn boundary, one short line — and MUST NOT duplicate the banner, journey map, before/after framing or step overview the loaded step then produces (INV-028–INV-031 unaffected, and the transition question is still asked exactly once — INV-006). This binds **every** site that acts on an affirmative transition or graduation reply, and such sites MUST name the file that defines the ordering rather than restating it (INV-179). ⛔ **"Acknowledge before proceeding" was already required and did not reach this.** `ground-rules.md` has carried that clause, including an explicit sub-case for bare readiness signals like `yes`, throughout — and it is satisfiable by one combined reply everywhere the next step is *composed*. It is not, where the next step must first be *loaded*. On 2026-08-25 a Bootcamper answered the Module 7 transition question, saw nothing across a skill invocation and two file reads, interrupted, and answered a second time: *"I lost my place and had to re-confirm."* From their point of view an unacknowledged interval is indistinguishable from an answer that never registered (INV-012), and the question was effectively asked twice without the guide ever re-asking it. ⚠️ **Compliance is not statically testable** — this governs what happens in a live turn, and `dry-run` phase 3 is the only check on it. `tests/test_acknowledge_precedes_the_loading_it_precedes.py` asserts the rule **ships** at every site that acts on an affirmative reply, and says so in its docstring rather than implying more. (Source: `the-acknowledge-rule-does-not-reach-across-the-module-transition`, 2026-08-26; registered 2026-08-27.)
invariants.summary: Where proceeding from a Bootcamper's answer requires **LOADING** anything — invoking a skill, reading a file, running a script — the acknowledgment of that answer MUST be emitted as bootcamper-visible text **BEFORE** the first such call, never composed into the reply that follows it.

invariants.statement: An assertion about **Senzing** — including non-technical assertions about the company, its licensing, support, pricing, internal process, or how its customers or employees operate — MUST come from an MCP tool, a shipped skill file, or something measured on this machine. There is no fourth source. The pre-response checklist's technical enumeration (SDK method names, attribute names, config options, error codes, entity-resolution technical details) is a **floor** and MUST NOT be read as the exhaustive set of claims requiring a source. An assertion that cannot be sourced MUST be **labeled as an inference at the point it is made, or MUST NOT be made**: a label attached to an advisory that should not have been offered does not satisfy this, and **at a gate the Bootcamper has already answered the required action is silence**. The labeling half applies where the Bootcamper *asks* something the plugin cannot source; it does not authorize volunteering. ⛔ **The enumeration is what caused this.** On 2026-08-25 the guide volunteered that Senzing employees *"very likely have access to a license through internal channels"* — its own inference about a business practice — in the same paragraph as the one-per-email and 30-day terms, which **were** sourced from the MCP server. Sourced and unsourced arrived together, indistinguishable, and no rule reached the sentence because a claim about business practices is none of the things the checklist lists. (**Widens INV-080** from Senzing *technical facts* to Senzing *assertions*; INV-080's own text repeats the same technical enumeration, which is why citing it at the new rule is not the same as registering the wider scope.) Enforced by `tests/test_sourcing_reaches_beyond_technical_facts.py`. (Source: `an-unsourced-inference-about-the-bootcamper-steered-a-consent-gate`, 2026-08-26; registered 2026-08-27.)
invariants.summary: An assertion about **Senzing** — including non-technical assertions about the company, its licensing, support, pricing, internal process, or how its customers or employees operate — MUST come from an MCP tool, a shipped skill file, or something measured on this machine.

invariants.statement: The Bootcamper's **identifying context** — name, email address, account details — is collected for identification and for fields a tool explicitly requires, and MUST NOT be used as a premise in the guide's reasoning about what the Bootcamper should choose. Employer, affiliation, seniority and entitlement MUST NOT be inferred from an email domain or any other identifying detail, and no such inference may steer a decision. An email address supplied to identify someone is not evidence about what options they have. ⛔ **Observed at the worst possible place (2026-08-25).** At the Module 4 License Key gate a Bootcamper chose *"request a free evaluation license now through the bootcamp"*. Before any value was collected the guide volunteered that their account email was on the `senzing.com` domain and that *"if you're at Senzing, you very likely have access to a license through internal channels"* — steering a decision they had made one turn earlier, at the only step in the bootcamp that transmits their personal details off their machine. Their words: *"I don't want assumptions presented as fact."* (**Distinct from INV-065**, which governs what **leaves the machine** in a bug report — identifiers stripped — and is silent on what may be *inferred from what stays*. Module 4 sub-step 6a already states that INV-065's stripping cannot apply to the license call, which does not work without those details, so the collection side was governed and the reasoning side was not. Also distinct from **INV-247**, which requires every 👉 question to trace to a shipped step: nothing was *asked* here.) Enforced by `tests/test_sourcing_reaches_beyond_technical_facts.py`. (Source: `an-unsourced-inference-about-the-bootcamper-steered-a-consent-gate`, 2026-08-26; registered 2026-08-27.)
invariants.summary: The Bootcamper's **identifying context** — name, email address, account details — is collected for identification and for fields a tool explicitly requires, and MUST NOT be used as a premise in the guide's reasoning about what the Bootcamper should choose.

invariants.statement: Where the guide refines a Bootcamper's answer into a **durable artifact that later modules read as an input**, the Bootcamper's original wording MUST be preserved beside the refinement, and the confirmation gate for that artifact MUST present **both** and state that a mismatch between them is what it is asking about. Refinement is not transcription: a gate shown only the refinement asks whether plausible text sounds right, not whether it matches what was said, and a single substituted word inside an otherwise-accurate sentence survives it. Where an answer was a selection from a **fixed vocabulary** the quote MUST be omitted rather than invented — an invented "verbatim" line is worse than none, because it looks like evidence. Where the answer is **already persisted** (e.g. `integration_targets` under INV-097) the quote MUST be taken from the persisted value rather than reconstructed, which makes that section's drift mechanically checkable.
