Downstream consumers continue to read the **refined** text and MUST raise a discrepancy rather than choosing a side when the two disagree. ⛔ **One adjective is the whole failure mode.** On 2026-08-25 a Bootcamper said their **possible**-fraud entities should feed the fraud tool; `docs/business_problem.md` rendered it as *"Internal fraud tool (**confirmed fraud cases**)"* — a different routing rule, changing which entities reach the tool and how large that queue is. Four lines earlier the same document still said *"Possible-fraud entities routed to the internal fraud tool"*, so **it contradicted itself and carried nothing that could settle which reading was right.** It was confirmed as accurate at the gate, then propagated three modules on: Module 7 step 1 derived requirement 7 as *"Confirmed-fraud candidate list"*, which the Bootcamper also approved — reviewing, again, only the refined artifact. ⚠️ **Scoped to `docs/business_problem.md` at registration.** Widening it to other module write-ups is a separate decision with its own cost in document length, and this invariant does not make it. Enforced by `tests/test_business_problem_preserves_the_original_wording.py`. (Source: `business-problem-keeps-only-the-refined-wording-so-the-gate-cannot-catch-drift`, 2026-08-26; registered 2026-08-27.)

A helper that reads a **bootcamper-owned artifact** MUST distinguish **absent** from **present but unreadable**, and MUST NOT collapse the two into one falsy result. Any caller that goes on to **write** that artifact MUST refuse and report when the read was unreadable, and MUST NOT proceed on a value that merely looks empty — rewriting a file whose existing content could not be read destroys it. The refusal MUST name the file and the cause, and MUST leave the artifact **byte-identical**; the plugin MUST NOT silently transcode or lossily re-read a document the bootcamper owns, because how it should be repaired is theirs to decide. ⛔ **The obvious fix is the data-loss bug.** `recap_checkpoint._read` caught `OSError` only, and `UnicodeDecodeError` derives from `ValueError`, so a cp1252 recap — what a Windows editor writes the moment prose carries a smart quote — crashed the PreCompact, SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks with a raw traceback. Widening that `except` to return `None` converts the crash into **silent destruction**: `fold()` treats the recap as empty and rewrites it in `"w"` mode with the current checkpoint block alone. Measured before the guard existed: a 279-byte recap holding **two completed module sections became 98 bytes holding none**, and the hook printed `folded … (97 characters)` — a success line — while doing it. ⚠️ **This is why the guard's assertion must be byte-identity, not absence-of-traceback:** a test asserting only that no hook crashed **passes** against the destroying patch, certifying the worse of the two bugs. Enforced by `tests/test_undecodable_recap_is_never_overwritten.py`, whose byte-identity and surviving-section assertions are what separate a correct fix from a destructive one. (Source: `a-non-utf8-recap-crashes-three-hooks-and-the-obvious-fix-destroys-it`, 2026-08-27; registered 2026-08-27.)
invariants.summary: A helper that reads a **bootcamper-owned artifact** MUST distinguish **absent** from **present but unreadable**, and MUST NOT collapse the two into one falsy result.

invariants.statement: A step that **GENERATES** a dataset or scenario for the Bootcamper MUST bound its default size, and MUST state the downstream time cost — naming the modules that absorb it — before generating anything larger on request. The larger scenario MUST still be generated: the bound is a default the Bootcamper may exceed, never a gate (INV-006, INV-251). The statement MUST NOT carry a wall-clock or throughput figure, which the generating step cannot know, and MUST NOT be tied to license capacity, which nothing has measured at that point (INV-093). ⛔ **The cost is not paid where the choice is made.** On 2026-08-25 a Bootcamper offered a 3-source, ~7,081-record scenario said it *"doesn't seem enough"* and was given a 5-source **~93,999-record** one with no statement of what that costs; the wait lands in Data collection, Data processing and Query/Visualize/Discover, by which point the decision is many steps behind and expensive to reverse. Enforced by `tests/test_generated_scenario_is_bounded.py`. (Source: `scenario-generation-has-no-size-cap-or-load-time-warning`, 2026-08-28.)
invariants.summary: A step that **GENERATES** a dataset or scenario for the Bootcamper MUST bound its default size, and MUST state the downstream time cost — naming the modules that absorb it — before generating anything larger on request.

invariants.statement: A bootcamp state field whose authority rests on being **measured** MUST be written only from that measurement, never from a Bootcamper statement, and no step may infer from the field's **presence** that a measurement was taken. A stated-but-unverified value MUST be recorded under a separate key that no gate reads. Where a later step can perform the measurement, it MUST reconcile the recorded value against it, **persist** the result, and say plainly when a recorded figure is withdrawn. ⛔ **The consequence is a suppressed warning, not a wrong number.** On 2026-08-25 a Bootcamper's stated 100,000-record entitlement was written into `license_record_limit` against an install measuring **500**; a value above the dataset size **suppresses** Module 4's Step 8a gate, the single volume-gated prompt in the bootcamp, on a ~94,000-record scenario. ⚠️ **A correction that stays on screen is not a correction** — the reconciling step must write it down, or the gate reads the disproved figure anyway. (**Extends INV-244** from the absent branch to the present one: INV-244 forbids reading absence as a finding; this forbids reading presence as a measurement.) Enforced by `tests/test_license_limit_is_written_only_from_a_measurement.py`. (Source: `license-record-limit-has-a-detected-only-contract-nothing-enforces`, 2026-08-28.)
invariants.summary: A bootcamp state field whose authority rests on being **measured** MUST be written only from that measurement, never from a Bootcamper statement, and no step may infer from the field's **presence** that a measurement was taken.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: A step that compiles code obtained from `generate_scaffold` MUST verify, **before invoking the compiler**, that every package the snippet imports is satisfiable by the installed environment, and MUST resolve an unsatisfiable **non-SDK** dependency by substituting only non-Senzing code — never by altering an SDK call, a flag constant or a method signature — recording the substitution in the saved file's header. The verification MUST be per-install rather than assumed, and the safety asymmetry (replacing the JSON library is safe; altering the SDK calls is not) MUST be stated **at** each such step rather than only cross-referenced (INV-183). ⛔ **The selection rule routes toward the dependency.** On server 1.33.0, 2026-08-28, **six of the six** Java `loading/` snippets that read an input file import `javax.json`; the only one without it hardcodes its records, which the steps forbid picking. `javax.json` is not in Java SE and no jar in a `senzingsdk-runtime` install provides it. Enforced by `tests/test_java_json_dependency_gap_is_covered.py`. (Source: `system-verification-java-loading-scaffold-hits-the-json-p-gap-too`, 2026-08-28.)

A tool's **declared schema** is authoritative for the **parameters it accepts** and MUST NOT be treated as authoritative for **prose describing what it covers** — repository counts, indexed file types, language or workflow lists. For coverage, `get_capabilities` governs, and a disagreement between the two MUST be settled by **making the call** rather than by preferring the text that looks newer. A coverage figure the server states two different ways MUST NOT be quoted in shipped guidance at all. ⛔ **The stale half carries the more official-looking citation.** On server 1.33.0 the `find_examples` manifest description omits `.ts`/`.js` and TypeScript while `get_capabilities` includes them; a live `language='typescript'` search returns a `.ts` file, so the declared half is stale — and it is the half sitting inside the artifact INV-234 makes authoritative. (Extends **INV-234** from what a tool accepts to what it is said to cover.) ⚠️ **Correction, 2026-09-02 — the ILLUSTRATING EXAMPLE was resolved upstream; the RULE is unchanged and is NOT retired.** The `find_examples` disagreement above was reported upstream 2026-08-27 and the server acted on it: re-checked on **server 1.36.0, 2026-09-02**, the declared description and `get_capabilities` now agree on repository count, indexed extensions and languages. Read the 1.33.0 sentences above as dated history, not as current state. The rule survives its example for two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one: a declared description's coverage prose is still not normative, and a coverage figure is **volatile server-side state** — it moves as the index grows, so a figure pinned in shipped guidance goes stale on the server's schedule whether or not two sources currently conflict. **The live illustration is now a different pair:** `search_docs`' declared description says the corpus is *"~2175 chunks"* while every response carries `metadata.documents_indexed: 14637` — plausibly different units rather than a contradiction, and **the tool documents neither**, which is precisely a coverage figure a caller cannot act on. ⛔ **Do not re-pin this invariant to whichever pair is current** — the wording above is the property; the examples are dated evidence beneath it, and the next resolution should cost a correction note rather than a rewrite. Enforced by `tests/test_find_examples_coverage_is_uncitable.py`. (Source: `find-examples-self-describes-two-different-coverages`, 2026-08-28; corrected by `find-examples-coverage-disagreement-was-fixed-upstream`, 2026-09-02.)
invariants.summary: A tool's **declared schema** is authoritative for the **parameters it accepts** and MUST NOT be treated as authoritative for **prose describing what it covers** — repository counts, indexed file types, language or workflow lists.

invariants.statement: The `Upstream:` outcome vocabulary is a closed set, and **every** site stating it — shipped or maintainer-side — MUST state the same values. A **consented** send that could not be made MUST carry its own value, distinct from a declined one, because the two differ in whether a report is still owed: a decline ends the obligation and a blocked send keeps it. ⛔ **The nearest wrong value misrecords consent.** A `/dry-run` forbids calling `submit_feedback`, so a Bootcamper's *yes* cannot be acted on; recording that as `offered, declined` states the opposite of what happened and reads as *considered and rejected* to whoever later decides whether the report is still owed. (Mirrors **INV-248** for the routing taxonomy; the asymmetry between the two is what allowed this set to drift — the routing taxonomy was bound and this one was not.) Enforced by `tests/test_blocked_submission_has_a_vocabulary_value.py`. (Source: `the-upstream-outcome-vocabulary-is-an-unbound-closed-set`, 2026-08-28.)
invariants.summary: The `Upstream:` outcome vocabulary is a closed set, and **every** site stating it — shipped or maintainer-side — MUST state the same values.

invariants.statement: A guard enforcing a rule across shipped prose MUST derive its matcher from the **CLAIM** being made, not from the phrasings observed at the sites it was written to fix. Where the claim can be made about a subject established in an earlier sentence, the matcher MUST NOT require that subject adjacent to it; scope by file instead. Every phrasing that has actually shipped MUST be pinned as a fixture, and every construction the matcher must **NOT** flag MUST be pinned beside it — a guard that flags correct prose is relaxed rather than fixed. ⛔ **Five instances in one day, three of them at one remove.** A writer count was wrong; the correction minted a new count; the guard against counts enumerated the phrasings already seen; the concept-level rewrite over-matched a compound adjective (`a stdlib-only writer`); and the *other* regex in the same file then enumerated the absence phrasings already seen, missing a site whose only difference was *which* against *what*. Each fix was right about its instance and reproduced the shape one level up. (**Extends INV-246** from a guard's set of FILES to its set of PHRASINGS: both fail by inheriting the blind spot of whoever last fixed the instances.) Enforced by `tests/test_license_limit_is_written_only_from_a_measurement.py` and `tests/test_new_hard_rules_are_cited_or_deferred.py`. (Source: `the-writer-count-matcher-enumerates-phrasings-not-the-concept`, 2026-08-28.)
invariants.summary: A guard enforcing a rule across shipped prose MUST derive its matcher from the **CLAIM** being made, not from the phrasings observed at the sites it was written to fix.

invariants.statement: A platform- or language-scoped value an MCP route returns — an environment variable, a path, an example command — MUST be attributed to the platform or language whose response returned it, **at the site it is presented**, and MUST NOT be presented as neutral guidance. Where the Bootcamper's own pair has no such value from any route, the step MUST say so and supply that pair's form as an **observation** (INV-080/INV-149) rather than leaving another platform's value standing as the only example. ⛔ **An accurate quotation of the wrong platform's response is the failure shape, and it does not look like one.** SDK setup presented `java -cp "${SENZING_ROOT}/sdk/java/sz-sdk.jar:…" MyApp` as *"the MCP install guidance's example"* — a verbatim, correctly-sourced quotation of the `macos_arm` Java `gotchas[]` entry, with nothing marking it as macOS-only. `SENZING_ROOT` is set by the macOS install and by nothing on `linux_apt`, so on Linux the example expands to `-cp "/sdk/java/sz-sdk.jar"`, every `com.senzing.sdk` import fails to compile, and the error surfaces in **System verification** — one module downstream, where it reads as a broken SDK install rather than a wrong classpath. ⚠️ **The absence half is what makes attribution insufficient on its own:** `sdk_guide(topic='install', platform='linux_apt', language='java')` returns no jar path, no `SENZING_ROOT` and no Java `gotchas[]` entry, and is byte-identical to the same call with no `language` argument (server **1.35.1**, 2026-08-31) — so a step that merely labels the macOS example still leaves the Linux reader with no path at all, which is why the pair's own form is required. (**Sibling to INV-194**, which forbids concluding the server lacks a fact from the wrong tool's empty response; this governs what to do with a fact the server returns for **one pair only**. **Complements INV-002**: language-agnosticism is about not privileging a language, this is about not silently generalizing one platform's answer.) Enforced by `tests/test_classpath_root_is_platform_qualified.py`. (Source: `java-classpath-guidance-is-macos-sourced-and-unusable-on-linux`, 2026-08-31.)
invariants.summary: A platform- or language-scoped value an MCP route returns — an environment variable, a path, an example command — MUST be attributed to the platform or language whose response returned it, **at the site it is presented**, and MUST NOT be presented as neutral guidance.

invariants.statement: Every option a **pinned gate** offers MUST have a handling step: a section in the same skill file, or an inline branch at the gate, saying what the guide does when that option is chosen and where the flow resumes. A gate whose option ends the turn with nothing to execute is **unsatisfiable**, and forces the guide to improvise against wording INV-056 pins precisely so it cannot drift. Where the handling step changes the state the gate measured, **re-presenting the gate with the new value is NOT an INV-006 repeat and MUST NOT be suppressed as one** — the state changed, so it is a new question about a new state. ⛔ **Observed live on 2026-08-28**: both Module 5 quality gates offered *"improve the data first"*, the Bootcamper chose it on a source scoring **75.1**, and no step in the plugin defined what happens next — the file ran from the pinned question to *"Success indicator"* and Phase 1 ended. ⚠️ **The re-present clause is load-bearing rather than a detail:** without it a guide honoring INV-006 suppresses the re-scored gate, and the improve path dead-ends one step later than it did before. ⚠️ **A handling step may be a heading or an inline branch, and both ship today** — Module 5 Phase 2 discharges its iterate options with `### 17. Iterate` while Phase 3 discharges its own inline (*"If rejected: … return to Phase 2 to adjust their mapping"*) — so a guard requiring one shape would report correct prose. (**Complements INV-247**, which binds where a question comes from — the ask side — and stops at the answer. **Complements INV-056**, which pins the wording of the ask and says nothing about the answer.) Enforced by `tests/test_gate_options_have_handling_steps.py`. (Source: `the-quality-gates-improve-option-has-no-procedure-and-is-incoherent-on-a-generated-scenario`, 2026-08-31.)
invariants.summary: Every option a **pinned gate** offers MUST have a handling step: a section in the same skill file, or an inline branch at the gate, saying what the guide does when that option is chosen and where the flow resumes.

invariants.statement: Where a provenance label — MCP-sourced, environment observation, or unknown — covers **several facts that can move independently** (per platform, per binding, per tool), it MUST be stated **per fact**, each with its own route and date. A blanket caveat over a set has **no way to become half-true**: when one member's provenance changes, the label becomes wrong for that member while continuing to read as reviewed for all of them. ⚠️ **The direction of the error does not matter.** Mislabeling a *served* fact as a local observation removes the reader's reason to re-ask the authority; promoting an *observed* fact to MCP-sourced because a sibling was promoted asserts a lookup nobody performed. ⚠️ **INV-080 and INV-149 were both considered and rejected as the citation for this rule** — INV-080 states that Senzing facts come from MCP, INV-149 governs empty `response_schemas` results; neither says anything about the *granularity* at which provenance is recorded, which is the whole rule here. Enforced by `tests/test_build_version_provenance_is_per_platform.py`. (Source: `szbuildversion-windows-path-is-now-mcp-sourced`, 2026-09-01.)
invariants.summary: Where a provenance label — MCP-sourced, environment observation, or unknown — covers **several facts that can move independently** (per platform, per binding, per tool), it MUST be stated **per fact**, each with its own route and date.

invariants.statement: A 👉 question whose options are **complements rather than alternatives** MUST be asked as a multi-select, using the plugin's single comma-separated idiom rather than a second shape, and **every option the Bootcamper selects MUST be recorded in full** wherever that answer is persisted or rendered. A multi-valued answer MUST NOT be narrowed to its first element at any point downstream. ⚠️ **The cost is not the lost option; it is the requirement invented in its place.** `docs/business_problem.md`'s Desired Output feeds Module 7 step 1's query requirements, so "1 and 3" written up as `Master list` becomes a requirement the Bootcamper never gave and then approves at Module 7, reviewing only the narrowed artifact. ⚠️ **INV-097 was considered and rejected as the citation for this rule** — it governs the integration and deployment questions and their persistence to `config/bootcamp_preferences.yaml`, not the desired-outcome answer. Two draft citations to it were written and then removed: a plausible-but-wrong citation is the INV-076/INV-077 defect class this repo has already paid for, and is worse than an honest deferral. Enforced by `tests/test_question_options_render_beneath.py`. (Source: `desired-outcome-question-is-single-select-for-a-multi-valued-answer`, 2026-09-01.)
invariants.summary: A 👉 question whose options are **complements rather than alternatives** MUST be asked as a multi-select, using the plugin's single comma-separated idiom rather than a second shape, and **every option the Bootcamper selects MUST be recorded in full** wherever that answer is persisted or rendered.

invariants.statement: Where the SBCP ships a rule into an artifact the Bootcamper works through **unattended** — a checklist, a migration item, a standing instruction they act on without the guide present — and that rule has a **known site where following it is wrong**, the exception MUST ship in the same item as the rule. ⛔ **Recording the exception in another document is not shipping it**: the reader of a checkbox does not follow a cross-reference before ticking it, and an unqualified rule is at its most damaging exactly where nobody is watching. Where the exception cannot be stated in the item, the item MUST be narrowed until it is true as written, never shipped broad with the correction elsewhere. ⚠️ **Distinct from INV-183**, which governs where a *citation* goes — a step naming the rules that govern the artifact it generates. This governs whether an *exception* travels with the rule it qualifies; neither implies the other. ⚠️ **Registered 2026-09-02 with no enforcing test, guarded 2026-09-02.** The note recording that gap is kept because the gap was real and the fix is dated: `tests/test_checklist_items_ship_their_exceptions.py` now asserts the exception sits inside the **quoted** checklist item, which is the only part copied into the Bootcamper's file — an exception in the guidance around it satisfies a reader of the skill and reaches nobody ticking the box. Enforced by `tests/test_checklist_items_ship_their_exceptions.py`. (Source: `export-flags-are-not-documented-against-the-export-method`, 2026-09-02.)

Where a generator lifts a **fenced region** out of a document, the region's terminator MUST be the one belonging to its own opening marker: a fence's span MUST NOT extend past the next opening marker of the same type. ⛔ **A malformed fence MUST NOT cost content the fence was not opened around.** Where the two cannot be reconciled, the generator MUST keep the content and **report the malformed marker by name** — never resolve the ambiguity by deleting. ⚠️ **A content-loss gate MUST measure against what the parse path actually kept**: a region excluded from the rendered output and from the source denominator alike is invisible to it, which is how a recap that lost a finalized module reported **94 percent retention and no error**. ⚠️ **Reconciles with INV-258**, which states that an unterminated fence runs to end of text: that fallback governs the case it was written for — a write truncated mid-fold, where the opening marker is the last one in the document — and applies **only where no well-formed span of the same type exists anywhere**. Where one does exist it wins; the stray START is left in place and reported by name, because sweeping to end of text would delete every module between the two markers. `_extract_notes_block` implements exactly this ordering. Enforced by `tests/test_recap_checkpoint_is_lifted_before_module_parsing.py`. (Source: `a-stray-fence-marker-silently-deletes-finalized-recap-modules`, 2026-09-02.)
invariants.summary: Where a generator lifts a **fenced region** out of a document, the region's terminator MUST be the one belonging to its own opening marker: a fence's span MUST NOT extend past the next opening marker of the same type.

invariants.statement: Where a reference implementation is reused by instruction — *"model it on X"* — any part of it whose correctness depends on the **scale or shape of the data it was written against** MUST be named at the point of reuse, and the strategy the new context requires MUST be stated rather than left to resemblance. ⛔ **A model built by enumerating a known input set MUST NOT be presented as complete**: it can only contain entities reachable from that input, so where the engine can enumerate the result set directly (an export stream) that is the source of truth for "every resolved entity". ⚠️ **The speed difference is what gets noticed and the completeness difference is what costs**: a per-record build of a Bootcamper's data made 19,584 round trips *and* silently omitted embedded-master records that appear in no input file — entities the module exists to show. ⚠️ **This binds BOTH ends of a reuse, not only the one that changes strategy.** The site where the reference is correct must say so and say what it is scoped to; a module that states its build flatly hands the guide an instruction that travels. Registered 2026-09-02 with `module-03b-truthset-visualization` brought into line in the same commit, because an invariant standing unmet at one of its own sites is how INV-097 and INV-060 each went unimplemented for weeks. Enforced by `tests/test_visualization_model_build_scales.py`. (Source: `visualization-model-build-does-one-get-entity-per-record`, 2026-09-02.)

Where two sources report the **same fact about the Bootcamper's environment** and can disagree, the guide MUST resolve by the **cause** of the disagreement, never by a fixed precedence between the sources. A formatting difference is normalized; a substantive difference means the sources describe **different things**, and the one describing what the system will actually *use* wins. ⛔ **An empty result from one source is not a finding about the fact** — it means that source does not own it (**extends INV-244** from a bootcamp state field to an environment probe). ⚠️ **A precedence rule generalized from one observation encodes that observation's only failure mode**: Step 1b's rule was written from a separator artifact and became a wrong version reported as fact on any install a package manager does not own — a route `sdk_guide` documents for containers, CI and no-sudo. ⚠️ **INV-269 is a specific instance of this**: the engine answers through the native library and the binding through the runtime's module search path, and the resolved path wins because it describes what actually loads. That rule stands on its own for binding verification and is not replaced; this states the general form, so a step comparing two environment sources has something to look up. ⚠️ **INV-163 was considered and rejected as the citation** — it governs a check that **cannot run** because its tool is absent, recorded as skipped. Here both sources answered and disagreed, which is a different subject. Enforced by `tests/test_version_precedence_handles_an_unmanaged_install.py`. (Source: `prefer-the-package-manager-version-is-wrong-for-an-unmanaged-install`, 2026-09-02.)
invariants.summary: Where two sources report the **same fact about the Bootcamper's environment** and can disagree, the guide MUST resolve by the **cause** of the disagreement, never by a fixed precedence between the sources.

invariants.statement: A **retrieval query whose result a step depends on** — a pinned list the guide is told to run, or a call whose output a branch reads — MUST be **measured against the live index before it ships**, and the list it belongs to MUST record the server version and **docs index date** the measurement was taken on. ⚠️ **Scope, stated because the broad reading is false at sites that are correct**: this does NOT bind an illustrative example of a tool's use, a query quoted as a **negative** example of what not to ask, or a pointer to a measured list elsewhere. None of those makes a claim about what comes back, and a rule that reads as binding them turns correct sites into apparent violations a later editor would "fix" (scope added at registration, 2026-09-02, after a sweep found 13 shipped files carrying a `search_docs` query and 5 of them out of scope). ⚠️ **The words in a query are not evidence about what it returns**: `search_docs` is BM25, so a well-formed, on-topic phrase using the right technical vocabulary can reach none of its material, and a query that misses is indistinguishable from documentation that does not cover the topic — which under INV-080 leaves the guide with nothing to say, or makes a training-data fallback feel justified. A guard over such a list MUST assert the **measured result**, never the query's vocabulary. (**Relates to INV-212**, which puts the retrieval strategy at the step; this is about whether the strategy's queries work.) Enforced by `tests/test_module_0_suggested_queries_are_measured.py`. (Source: `module-0-suggested-query-for-ambiguous-matches-misses-its-topic`, 2026-09-02.)

Where a provider supplies **more than one URL for the same content**, the bootcamp MUST prefer the route served to programmatic clients and say why, and every non-2xx MUST have a documented next step that distinguishes a **throttle** (retry with backoff) from a **refusal** (switch route — retrying cannot help). Where both routes fail, the guide MUST report the **host and status** rather than that the fetch failed. ⛔ **A client-identity workaround MUST NOT be instructed** — sending a User-Agent the client is not is the wrong habit to teach a bootcamp, and in the measured case does not even work. ⚠️ **A guarantee about a third-party host's access policy is an observation, never an MCP-sourced fact**: it MUST carry its date, the client it was measured with, and the machine's scope (INV-080/INV-149). ⚠️ **This binds every fetch step, not only the module the defect was found in.** Registered 2026-09-02 with `module-03b-truthset-visualization` brought into line in the same commit: it preferred the right route and documented the **throttle** (HTTP 429) but not the **refusal**, while instructing a fallback to the very URL measured to 403 — and it runs **before** the module carrying the remedy. A rule about non-2xx handling that covers one status is the half that fails silently. Enforced by `tests/test_cord_fetch_has_a_403_remedy.py`. (Source: `cord-source-download-url-403s-the-python-stdlib-client`, 2026-09-02.)

Where the bootcamp acquires data from a provider that places a **disclosure obligation on the caller**, that disclosure MUST be made to the Bootcamper **at every path that acquires the data, in the turn that acquires or binds it** — never deferred to a later module, and never converted into a 👉 gate (**INV-012**: they have already chosen the data; the disclosure asks nothing, and the two rules compose at every site — this one governs *what* must be said, INV-012 that it is a statement). For CORD specifically, `get_sample_data`'s contract requires stating that the records are **real**, are **historical snapshots**, and are for **evaluation rather than operational use**; describing them as synthetic, simulated or *"real-world-like"* is forbidden. ⚠️ **The Bootcamper's belief about whether the data is real governs how they treat it**, and in this plugin those names travel: Module 7 renders entity names, the screenshot flow embeds them in `docs/bootcamp_recap.md`, and graduation turns that into a keepsake PDF the Bootcamper is encouraged to share. Enforced by `tests/test_cord_is_disclosed_as_real_data.py`. (Source: `cord-is-described-as-real-world-like-but-the-server-says-it-is-real`, 2026-09-02.)

invariants.index_group: Data quality, mapping and validation gates
invariants.statement: Where a check classifies a source key as *structure* rather than as *content*, that classification MUST be decided by the key's **contents**, never by its name or shape, and any set of structural keys stated in the plugin MUST be closed rather than open-ended. A container whose contained keys do not resolve is unrecognized content, and its contents count toward the source's unrecognized set. ⚠️ **An open-ended list of examples is read as an invitation to add members by resemblance**, which is precisely how a gate that decides whether a whole module may be skipped comes to be satisfied by an array nobody dispositioned. Where a trailing `…` is kept, the text MUST say it continues *examples of the test* rather than members of the set. Enforced by `tests/test_coverage_check_looks_inside_root_arrays.py`. (Source: `step-5a-coverage-check-partitions-root-keys-only`, 2026-09-02.)
invariants.summary: Where a check classifies a source key as *structure* rather than as *content*, that classification MUST be decided by the key's **contents**, never by its name or shape, and any set of structural keys stated in the plugin MUST be closed rather than open-ended.

invariants.statement: A bootcamp state field measured from the environment **whose result can change once configuration a later step writes exists** MUST record **when** the measurement was taken alongside the value, and a step branching on it MUST NOT treat a reading taken before its inputs were complete as authoritative. ⚠️ **Scope, stated because the unqualified form is ceremony at two of the three fields it would bind**: a field whose value cannot move that way — `platform`, `database_type` — needs no marker, and requiring one there teaches that the marker means nothing, which is how a signal stops being read at the field where it does mean something (scope added at registration, 2026-09-02). Where a measurement's result depends on configuration a later step writes, the earlier reading is **provisional**: it MUST say so, a later step MUST re-take it once that configuration exists, and a superseded figure MUST be named aloud when it is replaced — including when the correction *raises* a limit, which is the direction most likely to be swallowed. ⚠️ **A measured-but-incomplete value is worse than an absent one**, because absence triggers a re-measure and presence suppresses it. (**Extends INV-278** on a new axis: INV-244 forbids reading *absence* as a finding, INV-278 forbids reading *presence* as a measurement, and this forbids reading a *measurement* as a complete one.) Enforced by `tests/test_license_limit_reading_is_complete.py`. (Source: `step-5a-measures-the-license-before-the-engine-config-exists`, 2026-09-02.)

Where a generated artifact's shape is selected from a recorded preference, **every** recorded input that constrains that shape MUST be read at the point of generation — not only the one the step is named for. Where a second input **narrows** what the first selected, the narrowing MUST be applied there and recorded **in the artifact itself**, naming what to restore it to when that input changes. A step that reads a constraining input only at a later gate ships an artifact tuned for conditions the Bootcamper does not have. ⛔ **The gate is not a substitute for the generation point**, even when it asks about the same thing: Data processing's Phase A selected the loader's worker count from the volume tier alone and read `database_type` only at the SQLite pre-load check further down, so answering "proceed on SQLite" kept a thread-pooled loader pointed at a datastore the server documents as having no concurrent writes — and graduation copies `src/load/**` into `production/` **verbatim**, so the mis-tuned artifact is inherited rather than corrected. Observed 2026-09-02 on Senzing SDK 4.4.0 (build 4.4.0.26242): 64 workers on SQLite, two engine `out of sync` diagnostics, throughput halving 854 → 485 rec/s, with the load itself correct. ⚠️ **Where the narrowing value is not served by any route, it is applied as the documented property's consequence and marked as a derivation** — `search_docs(query='loading', category='anti_patterns')` serves "tune based on your database and storage throughput" and SQLite's lack of concurrent writes, but no worker count (server **1.36.0**, 2026-09-02), so the ceiling is stated as derived rather than as documented (INV-080/INV-149). Enforced by `tests/test_loader_concurrency_reads_database_type.py`. (Source: `proceed-on-sqlite-keeps-the-tier-s-thread-count`, 2026-09-02.)
invariants.summary: Where a generated artifact's shape is selected from a recorded preference, **every** recorded input that constrains that shape MUST be read at the point of generation — not only the one the step is named for.

invariants.index_group: SDK usage: methods, flags and responses
invariants.statement: Output written by the **Senzing engine** MUST NOT be presented as, or conflated with, the plugin's own per-record outcome counts. Where a step directs the Bootcamper at console output, it MUST name which is authoritative for record failures — the loader's own `failed` count and its error log — and MUST give the reconciliation that settles a contradiction between them (records attempted equals records loaded, the redo queue reached empty, the error log absent or empty). An engine message the MCP corpus does not document MUST NOT be characterized at all, except as an environment observation carrying its SDK version and date (INV-080/INV-149). ⛔ **The failure shape is a Bootcamper reading `ERR:` beside "0 failed" with nothing saying the two are different things** — Phase B steps 6 and 7 both point at that console, and engine-level `[szstatic:…] ERR: Resolved entity … is out of sync` lines appear there during concurrent SQLite writes while the loader correctly reports zero record failures. This is narrower than **INV-265**, which governs whether the plugin's *own* checks establish non-empty input; this governs **attributing output to its writer**. Enforced by `tests/test_loader_concurrency_reads_database_type.py`. (Source: `proceed-on-sqlite-keeps-the-tier-s-thread-count`, 2026-09-02.)
invariants.summary: Output written by the **Senzing engine** MUST NOT be presented as, or conflated with, the plugin's own per-record outcome counts.

invariants.statement: A visualization view that **animates** to its final layout MUST expose a **settled signal** the capture can wait on: the server MUST remove `data-graph-settled` from the document element when it begins a layout, and set it to `1` when that layout has reached its final positions — **immediately, where there is nothing to lay out**, so a waiter on an empty graph is never left waiting. A screenshot of an animated view MUST be taken **after that signal** rather than on a fixed time budget alone, and a capture that proceeds without it MUST report that it did (INV-129). ⛔ **A time budget is not a settle guarantee, and a bigger one is not a better guarantee.** Measured 2026-09-03 on the full Truth Set (159 records → 85 entities, SDK 4.4.0 build 4.4.0.26242, 1440×900): five captures at the shipped 30 s animated-tab budget were byte-identical and five at 120 s produced the *same* image, while **five at 300 s produced two different images** — so the deadline does not select the layout and lengthening it made reproducibility worse, not better. ⚠️ **Real time is nearly flat across budgets** (0.6 s at 30 s vs 0.7 s at 300 s) because virtual time advances as fast as the page allows, so "raise the budget" costs almost nothing and buys almost nothing — which is why the signal, not the deadline, is the contract. This binds a server in **any** language (INV-002/INV-090), since a rule living only in the Python reference reaches no generated server. (Source: `graph-capture-budget-does-not-converge-at-truth-set-density`, 2026-09-03.)

A screenshot of an animated view MUST be produced by a **capture-oriented render**, requested explicitly (`?capture=1`), which drives the layout to completion **synchronously** rather than waiting on animation frames, **fits** the finished layout inside the viewport, and **suppresses on-canvas labels above a capture ceiling lower than the interactive one**. The **interactive** view MUST be unaffected: a real browser advances animation frames normally, so the defect this addresses is capture-only. ⛔ **Each of the three masked the next, and dropping any one re-breaks the artifact.** Measured 2026-09-03 through `capture_screenshots.py` on the full Truth Set (159 records → 85 entities, SDK 4.4.0 build 4.4.0.26242, 1440×900): the animation path advanced **5 of the ~300 ticks** the layout needs at every virtual-time budget from 5 s to 300 s, because d3's timer is driven by `requestAnimationFrame` and headless virtual time does not advance it — the nodes sat near their initial phyllotaxis positions, which look plausibly spread out, which is why it went unnoticed. Settling alone then put **most of the 85 nodes off-canvas**, because `forceCenter` centers the centroid and bounds nothing; the unsettled clump had been masking that. Fitting alone then rendered a 10 px label at the fit scale — **2–3 px**, a smudge rather than a name. ⚠️ **Suppress BOTH label sets through the app's own auto-off mechanism**, not a bespoke hide on one layer: the interactive ceiling governs entity names *and* match keys together, and reusing it keeps the on-screen toggles honest about what was drawn. The recap carries the entity names as text beside the image, so a dense captured graph's job is **structure**. This binds a server in **any** language (INV-002/INV-090), and pairs with **INV-298**, which is the signal that makes the finished state observable. (Source: `graph-capture-budget-does-not-converge-at-truth-set-density`, 2026-09-03.)

Where shipped guidance states that a rule, procedure or question's wording is **owned by one place** — *"stated once"*, *"the canonical statement"*, *"do not restate it here"*, *"cite it rather than restating it"* — that claim MUST name the owning file or step **and** the invariant that makes single-statement authoritative, and the pointing site MUST carry no second copy of the rule it points at. This binds whatever the rule governs: an artifact-generating step (where **INV-183** states it and continues to govern), an SDK error branch, a platform hazard, a license reconciliation, or a pinned question's wording. A copy that drifts is undetectable by construction — the duplication scan reports **exact** repeats, so two statements that have stopped matching are precisely what it cannot see. ⛔ **Scoped to a site that CLAIMS single-statement ownership**, not to every passage that could have restated a rule and did not: the wider form is unbounded and no guard could establish it, so it would be an invariant no test can hold (maintainer decision, 2026-09-03). ⚠️ **Extends INV-183's no-fork clause past its enclosing scope, and supersedes nothing.** INV-183 binds *"a step that instructs the guide to generate a bootcamper-facing artifact"*, so its *"named and linked, never restated or forked"* clause reached only artifact-generating steps — while the discipline was in use at roughly forty sites, twenty-seven of which cited no invariant at all and eight of which cited INV-183 for a clause whose scope did not reach them (`phase2-data-mapping.md:245`, a pinned question's wording, predates the 2026-09-03 citation sweep). Filed in this group beside INV-183 on the INV-268-extends-INV-132 precedent: an extension lives with its parent, so a reader arriving at either finds both. Enforced by `tests/test_a_single_statement_claim_names_its_authority.py`. (Source: `the-no-fork-discipline-is-registered-only-inside-inv-183s-artifact-scope`, 2026-09-03.) (⚠️ **What the enforcer establishes, stated 2026-09-03 — no meaning change.** The named test asserts the **citation** obligation and, for pointing sites, the **owner-naming** obligation; an owner-side declaration is exempt from the latter by its own wording. It does **not** assert that a pointing site carries no second copy of the rule. ⛔ **That clause is not a gap better regexes would close** — this invariant's own text says the duplication scan reports *exact* repeats, so a copy that has drifted is what it cannot see; establishing it means reading each pointer against its target, which is a person's work. The per-obligation table, the measurements behind it, and what the guard's vocabulary cannot see are in that test's module docstring, kept there so one statement of record stays authoritative rather than being restated here. Source: `the-inv-300-guard-checks-one-of-the-invariants-three-obligations`, 2026-09-03.) (⚠️ **Two sides, stated 2026-09-03 on the maintainer's approval — the pointing side is unchanged.** The obligations above describe the site that **points**. The **owner** side — a passage declaring *"this is the canonical statement"* — names no owning file because it **is** the owner, and *"no second copy of the rule it points at"* has no referent there. What it owes instead: it MUST **carry the rule in full** and MUST **cite this invariant**, so the discipline is discoverable from either end. Three such declarations exist today — module 2's env-script path-resolution rule, and module 4's overlap-preserving sampling rule and its three-checks CORD fetch rule — and their citations are kept, because removing them would leave one discipline reachable from one side only. ⛔ **Identified by file and section, never by line number:** an earlier form of this note named three `file:line` references, which put a list into an append-only file that nothing recomputes and every edit above them moves — the shape INV-244's writer count and INV-107's two-generator list each cost a correction note. ⛔ **The carry-in-full half is not assertable**, judging completeness being semantic; the cite-this-invariant half is asserted. Source: `inv-300s-notes-put-three-file-line-refs-in-an-append-only-file`, 2026-09-03.)

A release MUST move every record that asserts the version — the plugin manifest, every shipped file carrying a `**Plugin version:**` row, the `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and the git tag — as **one operation**, with no path that advances one without the others. The tooling MUST refuse, before writing anything, when the working tree is dirty, when the proposed version does not strictly advance the current one compared **numerically** (`0.5.10 > 0.5.9`), or when the tag already exists. ⛔ **The tag MUST be annotated**, because `git push --follow-tags` pushes annotated tags and **silently skips lightweight ones** — no warning, no error, exit 0 — so a release tag that never reaches the remote is invisible to the downstream repositories that port from a tagged release rather than from HEAD, which is the failure this rule exists to prevent. Measured 2026-09-14 in a throwaway repository carrying one tag of each kind: the annotated tag reached the remote and the lightweight one did not, with nothing in the output naming the omission. ⚠️ **All seven tags this repository carried before `release.py` are lightweight**, so this pins a NEW convention rather than an existing one. ⛔ The tag MUST point at the **release commit** rather than at HEAD, or it certifies a tree that does not carry the bump. Releasing MUST stop short of publishing: `/propagate-to-public` is a separate deliberate step, because coupling an irreversible local act to an outward-facing one removes the gate between them (maintainer decision, 2026-09-14). Filed in this group because it binds the development environment — the tooling lives under `.claude/`, which does not ship — so `coverage_reports.py shipped` is not expected to find it cited under `plugins/`. Enforced by `tests/test_release_bumps_version_changelog_and_tag_together.py` and `tests/test_release_covers_every_version_site.py`. (Source: `releasing-is-manual-and-the-steps-can-drift-apart`, 2026-09-14.)
invariants.summary: A release MUST move every record that asserts the version — the plugin manifest, every shipped file carrying a `**Plugin version:**` row, the `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and the git tag — as **one operation**, with no path that advances one without the others.

invariants.statement: The maintainer command surface MUST agree with its documentation in both directions and with the skills it fronts: every file under `.claude/commands/` MUST appear in `docs/development.md`, every command named there MUST exist, and every directory under `.claude/skills/` containing a `SKILL.md` MUST be fronted by at least one command. **Every entry in that documentation MUST carry a description**, since a bare name reads as an omission where every sibling entry has one. ⛔ The guard MUST compare **derived sets** and MUST NOT assert a count — a test pinning a number fails on the next legitimate addition and teaches whoever fixes it to bump it, reproducing inside the guard the staleness it exists to catch. ⚠️ **That clause is deliberately NOT assertable and is not claimed to be**, on the INV-300 precedent: it governs the guard's own source rather than the surface the guard reads, and any check would be brittle pattern-matching over another test's text. What IS asserted is its consequence — that the documentation states no count. Each direction fails differently and both matter: a documented command that does not ship tells the maintainer to run something that does not exist, one that ships undocumented is undiscoverable, and a skill fronted by nothing is reachable only by the model choosing it — the condition issues #18–#26 were each filed to remove, one command at a time. ⚠️ **The drift this prevents had already recurred twice**: the sibling guard for the bootcamper surface records it recurring once because a fix *"wrote the missing rows instead of pinning the set"*, and four PRs then corrected four maintainer-side rows one at a time in the same shape. A directory with no `SKILL.md` is not a skill and is excluded, which is why `implement-github-issue/` — run state, not a skill — does not demand a command. Filed in this group because it binds the development environment: the surface lives under `.claude/` and `docs/development.md`, so `coverage_reports.py shipped` is not expected to find it cited under `plugins/`. Enforced by `tests/test_documented_dev_commands_match_the_shipped_set.py` and `tests/test_dev_commands_name_a_real_skill.py`. (Source: `the-dev-command-list-has-drifted-from-the-shipped-set`, 2026-09-14.)

Every maintainer slash command under `.claude/commands/` MUST name, in its body, a skill that resolves to a directory under `.claude/skills/` containing a `SKILL.md`, and MUST NOT be silent about the skill it fronts. A command file is a thin front whose entire value is the indirection, and that is also its whole failure mode: a command whose skill has been renamed or removed still parses, still appears in the slash-command list, still reads as authoritative, and invokes nothing. `docs/development.md` demonstrated the class in prose before any command file did, listing `/compact-dev-development` and `/production-ready-review` against skills named `compact-dev-environment` and `production-readiness-audit`. The command's filename stem is NOT required to equal the skill it invokes, so an alias — two commands onto one skill with different defaults — stays available; that is a permission rather than an obligation, so no test asserts it. ⚠️ **Boundary with INV-302, which names the same enforcer and governs the mirror direction.** INV-302 binds the **sets** — command↔documentation in both directions, and skill→command, so every skill is fronted. **This binds the content of a command file** — command→skill, so every command names a skill that resolves. Neither implies the other: the phantom `/production-ready-review` was this direction, and the nine skills reachable only by the model choosing them were INV-302's. ⛔ **Stated because a reader arriving at either must find the other** — citing the set rule for a phantom-command defect, or the reverse, is the INV-076/INV-077 wrong-citation class, which has already cost this repo two corrections. Filed in this group beside INV-302 on the INV-300-beside-INV-183 precedent: an adjacent rule lives with its neighbor, so a reader arriving at either finds both. Enforced by `tests/test_dev_commands_name_a_real_skill.py`. (Source: `the-github-issue-path-ships-guarantees-with-no-invariant`, 2026-09-14.)
invariants.summary: Every maintainer slash command under `.claude/commands/` MUST name, in its body, a skill that resolves to a directory under `.claude/skills/` containing a `SKILL.md`, and MUST NOT be silent about the skill it fronts.

invariants.statement: The propagate mirror MUST NOT publish anything under `.claude/`: every source it reads MUST be one of the explicitly reviewed roots, and the check MUST compare **path components**, never string prefixes. The public repo ships a participant runtime, so publishing the maintainer half hands a bootcamper release-path tooling that acts on repos they do not have — and in the case of `retrofit-from-public` and `propagate-to-public`, tooling that writes across two checkouts. ⛔ **This held only by construction, not by rule**: `propagate.sh` happens to name its sources one at a time, and a future `rsync -a --delete "$here/" "$dest/"` to "simplify" the calls into one would publish the whole maintainer surface and still pass every other test in the suite. ⛔ **`.claude-plugin/` IS propagated and MUST stay propagated**: it holds `marketplace.json`, which is how the plugin is installed, and it string-prefix-matches `.claude`, so a guard written as `path.startswith(".claude")` fails on the very file the release depends on — which is why the comparison is by path component. ⚠️ **A new published root MUST be a reviewed decision**: the guard compares the parsed sources against the reviewed set as a ceiling as well as a floor, so adding a fifth root fails until it is named there in the same edit. That is deliberate — publishing a new path to a participant repo is the change that should be looked at rather than inferred. Filed in this group because it binds the development environment's release path rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_maintainer_tooling_stays_out_of_public.py`. (Source: `the-github-issue-path-ships-guarantees-with-no-invariant`, 2026-09-14.)
invariants.summary: The propagate mirror MUST NOT publish anything under `.claude/`: every source it reads MUST be one of the explicitly reviewed roots, and the check MUST compare **path components**, never string prefixes.

invariants.statement: `fpdf2` is optional by design and **both renderer paths ship**, so the test suite MUST be run under CI in two configurations — `fpdf2` present and `fpdf2` absent — and the absent configuration MUST **assert that `fpdf2` is genuinely unimportable before running**. ⛔ Without that negative control a transitively-installed `fpdf2` silently turns the absent job into a second copy of the present one: still green, and no longer testing the stdlib fallback, which is **the path most bootcampers hit**. The absent job MUST additionally require a notice naming `fpdf2` and a **non-zero skip count**, so guards that stop being applied surface as a failure rather than as a quiet pass — a run reporting zero skips there is the regression arriving silently. ⚠️ **Scope, stated because the enforcer asserts more than this rule does.** `tests/test_ci_workflow_guards_the_fpdf2_matrix.py` also pins six further CI guarantees that **no invariant currently records**: `shell: bash` on every piping step (without it there is no `pipefail`, so a failing suite piped to `tee` reports green), third-party actions pinned to a SHA, each pin naming its version in a comment, `fetch-depth: 0` on checkout (a shallow clone cannot resolve the commit hashes the ledger records, and a test depends on it), CI running `unittest discover`, and no propagate source reaching `.github/`. Those are a different subject — the CI workflow's own integrity, rather than the optional-renderer matrix — and folding them in would put two subjects in one permanent statement. They are named here so they are visible rather than silently unregistered (maintainer decision, 2026-09-14). Filed in this group because it binds the repository's own CI rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_ci_workflow_guards_the_fpdf2_matrix.py`. (Source: `the-github-issue-path-ships-guarantees-with-no-invariant`, 2026-09-14.)

invariants.statement: Every optional dependency the test suite can exercise MUST be declared in `requirements-dev.txt`, and tests that require it MUST **skip with a stated reason** rather than fail when it is absent. An undeclared optional dependency is invisible to anyone whose machine happens to have it, and its absence surfaces as a wall of domain assertions about unrelated behavior — **41 such failures were once read as product defects** when the only defect was an unstated prerequisite, and only 6 of them named the missing package anywhere in their traceback. The skip notice MUST name both the cause and the remedy, and ⛔ **MUST NOT state how many tests it affects** — a hardcoded count rots on the next legitimate addition and teaches its reader to bump it, the same habit INV-302's guards refuse by name. ⛔ **At least one test MUST actually apply the guard**, or the discipline is asserted over nothing: a decorator no file uses is indistinguishable from one that works. The manifest MUST be named in the contributor-facing documentation — `docs/development.md` and `tests/README.md` — since a prerequisite discoverable only by reading a traceback is not declared in the sense that matters. ⚠️ **Only genuinely-needing tests may be guarded**: several files deliberately exercise the **stdlib fallback**, which ships too and is the path most bootcampers hit, so guarding those would silently delete the coverage that matters most — the guards were applied against a measured list of failing test ids, not file by file. **Pairs with INV-305**, which binds the CI matrix that runs the suite with the dependency present and absent: this governs the declaration and the skip, that governs the two-cell run which proves both paths are exercised. Filed in this group because it binds the repository's own test apparatus rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_fpdf2_dependency_is_declared.py`. (Source: `the-github-issue-path-ships-guarantees-with-no-invariant`, 2026-09-14.)

invariants.statement: `specs/` MUST remain a **read-only archive** as of the 2026-09-15 cutover: new work is tracked as GitHub issues, and the frozen set MUST be pinned **by name** in `specs/FROZEN-MANIFEST.txt` and compared against the directory **in both directions**, with no count asserted anywhere. ⛔ The deletion direction is the load-bearing one and MUST NOT be dropped as redundant: `INVARIANTS.md` cites its sources by spec slug, and `tests/test_spec_ledger_invariants.py` satisfies such a citation with **either** a file under `specs/` **or** an entry in `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` — so removing a spec that happens to be ledgered breaks no other test while destroying the reasoning its invariant points at, and six citations already resolve through the ledger alone. ⛔ `IMPLEMENTED.md`, `DECLINED.md` and `INVARIANTS.md` MUST stay **live and outside the frozen set**, because appending to them is behavior the archive depends on — the ledger carries those six citations, and `/review-invariants` appends to `INVARIANTS.md` by design; a guard MUST assert they are absent from the manifest rather than leaving their exemption implicit. The cutover date MUST be stated in the directory itself, not only in a test, so the freeze stays datable by a reader who never runs the suite. Filed in this group because it binds the repository's own development record rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_specs_are_frozen.py`. (Source: `specs-is-frozen-and-the-cutover-date-is-recorded`, 2026-09-16.)

invariants.statement: A tool that reports a verification count MUST also report what it **could not** verify, and MUST distinguish *nothing to check* from *could not check it*. ⛔ A skip that increments no counter is invisible, and a run that verified nothing then reads exactly like a run that verified everything — the failure is silent, self-certifying, and reaches whoever trusts the output as a clean result. Where a location cannot be resolved the tool MUST name it, say the claim behind it is unverified, and state that the run is **not** clean; where nothing was available to check it MUST say the check was **empty** rather than passing. ⚠️ **The legitimate case MUST be counted separately from the failure**, or the warning fires on correct input and is learned as noise. ⛔ The roots or scope such a tool resolves against MUST have **one definition** that every consumer reads — including its own guards — since a second copy goes stale silently and passes until something first uses the new scope, which is how `conformance.py`'s widening shipped a stale guard on 2026-09-14 and how three copies of this resolver coexisted until #59. ⚠️ **A scope-narrowing that happens to produce correct behavior is not a rule and MUST NOT be relied on**: `cmd_sites` excluded non-citation paths only because they failed to resolve, and widening the roots silently undid it. Filed in this group because it binds the repository's own verification tooling rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_review_invariants_queue.py`. (Source: `pending-invariants-check-reports-a-clean-run-over-what-it-could-not-read`, 2026-09-16.)
invariants.summary: A tool that reports a verification count MUST also report what it **could not** verify, and MUST distinguish *nothing to check* from *could not check it*.

invariants.statement: Work taken through this repository's **issue-driven development path** — the command that carries a GitHub issue from reported to pull-request-open, currently `/implement-github-issue` — MUST NOT close its issue until the durable rules it ships are accounted for, by exactly one of three explicit answers: an invariant **registered**, a `DEFERRED INVARIANT` block **written** in `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` with its drafted wording and enforcer, or a plain statement that the work **establishes no invariant**. ⛔ Silence is not one of the three, and a bare "deferred" label with no drafted wording does not discharge the obligation — it records nothing a later reader can act on. ⛔ The command MUST NOT register an invariant itself: minting an ID is the maintainer's alone through `/review-invariants`, and the drafted id MUST be written as `INV-NNN`, since a literal number cites an invariant that does not exist and only the first block minted would get the id any pending block named. ⚠️ **The gate belongs to the command rather than to the skill**, because the skill has a copy outside this repository shared with projects that have no `INVARIANTS.md`, where the rule would be false. ⚠️ **A guard on this rule MUST assert the condition rather than the wording** (INV-219): that closing and the deferral mechanism appear in one requirement, and that all three answers survive — a guard demanding only registration would make the command claim a power it does not have. This is the mechanical form of the gap `the-github-issue-path-ships-guarantees-with-no-invariant` recorded: four durable guarantees shipped with enforcing tests and no registered invariant inside eleven days, and routing all development through one command raises the volume passing through it. (⚠️ **Amended before minting, 2026-09-16:** the draft bound `/implement-github-issue` **by name**. Every other rule in this group states a condition, and #51 is renaming a sibling command as this is written — so a named command would have stranded this invariant on the next rename, and `INVARIANTS.md` is append-only, meaning the repair would be a dated correction rather than an edit. The rule now binds the **path**; the command name is a dated pointer to it.) Filed in this group because it binds the repository's own development record rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_issue_command_gates_invariant_capture.py`. (Source: `the-issue-command-has-no-front-and-invariant-capture-is-not-gated`, 2026-09-16.)

A maintainer command that performs a **permanent or append-only** act on this repository's own records MUST stop at the working tree: it performs the change, verifies it, reports every file it touched, and MUST NOT commit or push. ⛔ Approving the **content** of such an act is not approving its **commit**, and the two MUST be separated by the tool rather than by the maintainer remembering — which is what made the gap easy to miss, since the maintainer is standing right there and approved the content a moment earlier. ⚠️ This generalizes what INV-301 states for **releasing** only — *"coupling an irreversible local act to an outward-facing one removes the gate between them"* — to the other acts of that kind, of which registering an invariant is the one that had **no gate at all**: `/review-invariants` said *"Verify, then commit"* and named no destination, so it committed onto whatever branch was checked out, which after a merge and pull is `main`. ⚠️ **A branch is not required and was deliberately not mandated**: the branch-name convention in force names branches `<issue-number>-<github-username>-<n>`, and a review session has no single issue — `invariant-review-2026-09-14` registered seven ids drawn from different sources — so requiring one would have required instructing a bypass of that convention. Stopping needs no branch. ⛔ **Deliberately NOT cited as INV-301 at its sites**: that invariant's subject is a *release*, and citing it would be the mis-citation the 2026-09-01 audit found, where a rule was counted as accounted-for because the sentence beside it cited invariants about something else. ⚠️ **Scoped to acts on this repository's own records at registration.** `/propagate-to-public` and `/retrofit-from-public` also stop at the working tree and are **outside** this subject — their act is outward-facing rather than permanent or append-only here — so they are recorded as considered and out of scope rather than left ambiguous; widening to cover them is a separate decision this invariant does not make. ⚠️ **A guard on this rule can only assert what the command INSTRUCTS**: no offline test can observe a run refraining from `git commit`. Filed in this group because it binds the repository's own development tooling rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_review_invariants_stops_at_the_working_tree.py`. (Source: `review-invariants-stops-at-the-working-tree`, 2026-09-21.)
invariants.summary: A maintainer command that performs a **permanent or append-only** act on this repository's own records MUST stop at the working tree: it performs the change, verifies it, reports every file it touched, and MUST NOT commit or push.

invariants.statement: Where this repository publishes a **derived** artifact for downstream ports to consume, the artifact MUST name its source, MUST be regenerable by a script in this repository, and MUST be checked against that source so it cannot drift. ⛔ **It is never authoritative: the prose it derives from is.** ⚠️ Where a field cannot be derived, the artifact MUST carry an explicit undetermined value **and MUST say in the artifact itself that undetermined means *not derivable*, never *absent*** — a consumer reading a null as absence under-counts its own register, and the file travels to other repositories without this one's documentation. ⚠️ **A guard on this rule can assert that the artifact matches its source; it cannot assert that a consumer reads it correctly**, which is why the meaning of an undetermined value is carried *in* the artifact rather than only in the parent's docs. ⛔ **The rule exists because the alternative was measured, not imagined**: without a published list the Kiro and Codex ports each had to parse a 398 KB prose file written for human authority, and each would have parsed it differently — defeating the uniformity their invariant-disposition registers exist for. ⚠️ **Two fields the first such artifact was asked for could not be derived at all** — 113 of 309 entries have no extractable one-line statement, and supersession is written six ways in the prose — so they are reported as undetermined and counted rather than guessed; that outcome is the rule working, not a shortfall in it. ⚠️ **Scoped to artifacts published for downstream consumption** at registration: a report a maintainer reads on screen is not one, and widening it to every generated file is a separate decision this invariant does not make. Filed in this group because it binds the repository's own development record rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_invariant_manifest_matches_the_prose.py`. (Source: `a-machine-readable-invariant-manifest-for-downstream-ports`, 2026-09-22.)
invariants.summary: Where this repository publishes a **derived** artifact for downstream ports to consume, the artifact MUST name its source, MUST be regenerable by a script in this repository, and MUST be checked against that source so it cannot drift.

invariants.statement: A maintainer command that brings **another repository's changes into this one** MUST NOT write them into the working tree: it compares, reports what diverged, and files GitHub issues describing it, ⛔ **in its own repository only**. Cross-repo filing is a different act with a different owner and MUST NOT be reachable from a sync command. ⚠️ **The reason is measurable rather than stylistic**: `tests/` is not in the public mirror and cannot come back, so a copied prose edit lands in a shipped file while the dev-only test quoting that sentence keeps asserting the old wording — measured 2026-08-16 on `2223961`, a **correct** edit, faithfully retrofitted, which left **12 failed / 2730 passed**. An issue makes the same change arrive where the suite is run and reconciled deliberately. ⚠️ **Any transform the sync used to apply becomes manual** and MUST be stated as work the filed issue owes, or the receiving repository accumulates the sending one's self-references. ⚠️ **A guard on this rule can only assert what the command instructs**: no offline test can watch a run refrain from copying, and the source repository is absent on some machines — so an `Enforced by` clause here is not a compliance claim. ⛔ **Registering this found two sites stating the OPPOSITE**, both left by the change that shipped the rule: the command's `description` still said it retrofits changes *"back into this development repo"* and told the reader to *"stop at the working tree"*, and the skill's own frontmatter still described copying — wording from before the rule existed. Both corrected at registration; the incompleteness, not the rule, is what the 2026-09-01 class predicts. Filed in this group because it binds the repository's own development tooling rather than anything a Bootcamper's guide reads. Enforced by `tests/test_retrofit_files_issues.py`. (Source: `retrofit-files-issues-instead-of-applying-changes`, 2026-09-22.)
invariants.summary: A maintainer command that brings **another repository's changes into this one** MUST NOT write them into the working tree: it compares, reports what diverged, and files GitHub issues describing it, ⛔ **in its own repository only**.

note: Derived, never authoritative. `summary` is null where no one-line statement could be extracted -- that means NOT DERIVABLE, never absence of a rule; `statement` always carries the full text. `status` is `unclear` where the prose's supersession wording is ambiguous, never guessed.
